The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    10 - Pierre Gasly
Competitor BWT Alpine F1 Team
Time           15:34
Session        Race
Fact           Contact occurred between Car 10 and Car 31 at Turn 3.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV Art 2(d) of the FIA International Sporting
             Code.
Decision       No further action
Reason         The Stewards reviewed video and in-car evidence.
               Car 10 (GAS) moved to overtake Car 31 (OCO) on the inside at Turn 3. A minor
               collision occurred between the two cars just after the apex.

               OCO’s car prior to and at the apex and Car 10 was driven in a fully controlled
               manner.

               Turn 3. However, OCO had already turned-in and was committed to the corner at the
               point where the collision occurred. The Stewards determined that no driver was wholly
               or predominantly to blame for the collision and for that reason took no further action.

No / Driver    12 - Kimi Antonelli
Competitor Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team
Time           16:16
Session        Qualifying
Fact           Alleged pitlane incident – Working on the car in the fast lane
Infringement Alleged breach of Article B1.6.1e of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards reviewed video evidence and determined as follows.
               During the Qualifying session, which was suspended due to a red flag incident, and
               while the cars were lined up to leave the pit lane, Car 12 was waiting to blend into the
               fast lane. Car 12 had inched slightly into the fast lane with a very small portion of the
               front wing in the fast lane. A team member assisted in pushing the car back a little to
               allow for that part to not hinder the fast lane.
               While the car was touched by the team member (to push it back), this did not
               constitute a breach of Article B1.6.1e which prohibits work being done on the car,
               which clearly was not the case here. In fact, the team member was taking steps to not
               hinder the other drivers in the fast lane, which was entirely appropriate in the
               circumstances.
               We accordingly took no further action.

 The Stewards have received a request from Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team to allow Car 18 to start
 the Race despite:

 - Failing to set a qualifying time within 107% of the fastest time set in Q1.

 In accordance with Article B2.4.3b of the FIA F1 Regulations, the Stewards have the power to grant
 permission if circumstances justify it. These circumstances include taking into account parameters
 where “a suitable lap time [has been] set in another practice session, the general performance of the
 driver in Competitions of the Championship…”

 The Competitor brought the following matters to the attention of the Stewards in seeking permission:

 • The driver of the second car from the team, Car 14, Fernando Alonso, demonstrated that the
 AMR26 was capable of qualifying within 107% of the fastest qualifying time;

  • The driver of Car 18, Lance Stroll:
. has completed a total of 859km so far this year in the AMR26;
. has competed in 178 F1 World Championship Grands Prix since making his debut in 2017;
. has competed in seven Australian Grand Prix races, achieving classification in six of those events,
  with a best result of 4th place in 2023, demonstrating significant familiarity with the circuit and its
  operational requirements
. has scored 325 career World Championship points, including podium finishes and one pole position.

 • The team also highlighted that they took the decision to not have Car 18 participate in Qualifying,
 due to a damaged oil line in the car, out of prudence, to enable them to undertake further
 investigations.

 Taking into account the reasons set out above, which the Stewards consider to be compelling, the
 Stewards grant permission for Car 18, Lance Stroll, to start the Race. The car will be placed on the
 grid in accordance with Article B2.5.4 of the FIA F1 Regulations.

 Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the Stewards, in
 accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial
 and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.
 Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely on the relevant
 regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 19) and
heard from the driver and team representative, have considered the following matter and determine
the following:

No / Driver    43 - Franco Colapinto
Competitor BWT Alpine F1 Team
Time           16:02
Session        Practice 2
Fact           Driving Unnecessarily Slow on the Main Straight
Infringement Alleged Breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 43 (Franco Colapinto), the team
               representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence.

               COL explained that his Car suffered a ‘false neutral’ as he was approaching the final
               turn and lost drive as he turned onto the main straight. While the Team were giving
               him instructions over the radio to attempt to resolve the issue, the Driver kept his Car
               rolling slowly on the left of the main straight having been instructed to do so by his
               Team should he be unable to resolve the issue and the Driver needed to stop the
               Car. As COL approached the control line, COL was caught by HAM. While HAM had
               a clear line of sight of COL for some distance along the main straight, HAM was
               apparently surprised to find COL moving so slowly on the racing line and had to take
               evasive action to avoid a collision.

               COL explained that he was watching his mirrors the whole time and knew that HAM
               was approaching. He said that he was instructed by the Team to stay to the left
               because the Race Director’s Competition Notes (Emergency Exit Map) marks the
               exit point on the main straight on the left side of the track. He said that if he had tried
               to move off the racing line when he had no drive he could have created a more
               dangerous situation.
               The Stewards were satisfied that there was nothing about COL’s driving which was
              erratic. Given his mechanical problem, he was not driving “unnecessarily” slowly.
              Given further that the Driver positioned his Car to ensure that he could reach the
              designated exit point in the event that the problem with his Car was not resolved
              before he reached it, the Stewards did not consider that the actions of the Driver
              were unsafe and therefore determined to take no further action.

              Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
              Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
              Chapter 4 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

              on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 36) and
heard from the team representative, have considered the following matter and determine the
following:

No / Driver    10 - Pierre Gasly
Competitor BWT Alpine F1 Team
Time           16:44
Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 10 was released from its garage in an unsafe condition.
Infringement Breach of Article B1.6.2 b) i) of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision       The Competitor (BWT Alpine F1 Team) is fined €5.000.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the team representative of Car 10 (Pierre Gasly) and
               reviewed video and in-car video evidence.

               The video evidence showed that, as the car was exiting its garage during the
               Qualifying session, a component from the left-front wheel assembly detached and
               rolled through the fast lane before coming to rest in the inner lane of the pit lane.

               The team representative acknowledged the mistake and apologised for the lapse. He
               explained that a mechanic had inadvertently failed to correctly secure the component
               during the preparation of the car, which resulted in the part detaching when the car left
               the garage. He further stated that the team had faced logistical challenges as not all
               parts had arrived in Melbourne in time, which meant that the team could not fully carry
               out its usual preparation procedures.

               The Stewards acknowledge the logistical challenges faced by the team. However, the
               responsibility for ensuring that a car is released from the garage in a safe condition
               rests with the Competitor. As a component detached from the left-front wheel
               assembly when the car exited the garage, the Stewards determined that the car was
               released in an unsafe condition.

               Having considered previous decisions for comparable infringements during
               Qualifying, the Stewards conclude that a financial penalty is appropriate. Accordingly,
               the Stewards impose a fine of €5,000 on the Competitor.

               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 37) and
heard from the team representative, have considered the following matter and determine the
following:

No / Driver    12 - Kimi Antonelli
Competitor Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team
Time           17:00
Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 12 was released from its garage in an unsafe condition.
Infringement Breach of Article B1.6.2 b) i) of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision       The Competitor (Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team) is fined €7,500.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the team representative of Car 12 (Kimi Antonelli) and
               reviewed video, team radio and in-car video evidence.
               Car 12 (Antonelli) was released from its garage during the session with a duct cooling
               fan still attached on the right side of the car. The fan assembly disconnected from the
               duct of Car 12 as it negotiated Turn 1, split apart and one section of it bounced off
               the track onto the gravel at the exit. Another section of the fan assembly dislodged
               onto the track at Turn 2 and was later struck by the front wing and tyre of another car
               causing debris to be strewn over the track, damage to the front wing of the other car
               and the session had to be red flagged to remove the debris.
               The Team explained that an incident in an earlier session in which Car 12 had
               sustained significant damage meant that the division of labour within the Team had to
               be changed to repair the damage within a short time frame. Usually, a separate team
               member would have responsibility for inserting and removing each fan but the need to
               address legacy issues from the earlier incident during the session meant that the
               team member responsible for the fan on that side of the car was occupied on another
               task and the removal of the fan before the car was released from the garage was
               missed.
               The Team (and the Driver) were unaware that the fan had not been removed until the
               incident was noted by Race Control.
               The Stewards determine that because Car 12 left its garage with a piece of
               equipment still attached, it was released in an unsafe condition and the Stewards
               impose a fine on the Competitor accordingly.

Fact           Car 63 performed a practice start outside the designated practice start area
Infringement Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code in combination with
             Item 14.1 of the Race Director Competition Notes (Document 8).
Decision       Driver: Warning.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 63 (George Russell) and the team
               representative and reviewed video evidence.
               The driver admitted that he performed a practice start outside the designated practice
               start area defined in Item 14.1 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes. However,
               he explained that, due to sun haze, he was unable to clearly see the grid boxes and
               believed that the correct location was where the rubber marks were visible on the
               asphalt.

               Having viewed the Driver’s onboard and CCTV footage, we accept that the sighting of
               the grid box was difficult given the light conditions but the Driver was so far forward
               from the designated location that it was ahead of the protection of the pit wall and this
               incident occurred after the Race Director had warned all Teams of the need to
               comply with his instructions in this regard.

               The Stewards determined that the driver failed to follow the Race Director’s
               instructions and impose a penalty consistent with the penalty for similar breaches in
               the past.
               The Stewards remind all Competitors that compliance with the Race Director’s
               instructions regarding the correct position from which to perform practice starts is
               imperative for the safe conduct of the Event.

              Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team
                                                                       Time         20:38


The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (documents 17 & 18)
and heard from the drivers and team representatives, have considered the following matter and
determine the following:

No / Driver    63 - George Russell
Competitor Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team
Time           16:00
Session        Practice 2
Fact           Pit Lane Incident with Car 41
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 5b of the International Sporting Code.
Decision       Driver: Reprimand
Reason         The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 41 (Arvid Lindblad) and the driver of Car
               63 (George Russell), the team representatives and reviewed video, team radio and
               in-car video evidence and determined that Car 41 was in the queue of cars in the fast
               lane waiting to get out of the pit lane.
               Car 63 left the garage and was waiting to join the fast lane. Car 63 inched forward, as
               if to join the fast lane and then stopped slightly ahead of Car 41, with a small portion
               of Car 63 jutting into the fast lane.
               This resulted in Car 41 running over that portion of the front wing end plate of Car 63.
               There was no damage reported to us in relation to Car 41 as a result of the collision.
               Appendix L Chapter IV of the FIA International Sporting Code read with the Race
               Director Competition Notes Item 15 gives priority to the cars in the fast lane over
               those in the working lane. In other words, Car 41 had priority over Car 63.

               Car 63 would only have been free to blend into the fast lane “if there [was] a suitable
               gap in a queue of cars in the fast lane” and if it could be done safely and without
               unnecessarily impeding cars already in the fast lane.
               It is clear, in this case, that there was no such gap and the collision resulted from Car
               63 inching forward and thereby blocking a small portion of the fast lane. Both drivers
               agreed that the driver of Car 41 would not have been able to see the portion that was
               blocking the fast lane.
               In this case, the collision could have been avoided by Car 63 taking appropriate
               action and we therefore imposed a penalty of a reprimand to the driver of Car 63.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
              Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
              Chapter 4 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.
              Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely
              on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     11 - Sergio Perez
Competitor Cadillac Formula 1 Team
Time            15:03
Session         Race
Fact            Car 11 moved prior to the start signal.
Infringement Breach of Article B5.11.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        No penalty is applied.
Reason          The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data and in-car video
                evidence.
                The car moved before the start signal was given. This normally warrants a 5 second
                penalty (which would not convert into a grid drop for the next race).
                However, as the car had already retired from the race at the time the incident was
                brought to the attention of the Stewards, it does not seem appropriate to apply any
                time penalty. Therefore the Stewards decide not to impose any penalty.

                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact            The Driver did not follow the Race Director’s instruction considering practice starts
                (item 13.6 of the Competition Notes) by crossing the white line at pit exit and
                subsequently cutting back in to make a practice start.
Infringement Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the International Sporting Code and non-compliance with
             Race Director’s Competition Notes (item 13.6, document 6).
Decision        No penalty is applied.
Reason          The Stewards reviewed in-car video evidence.

                stopped in the pit exit road. In the process of passing this car and then making way
                for it after it started moving, Car 30 crossed the white line at pit exit at slow speed.
                After that, Car 30 crossed the line again to line up for a practice start as originally
                planned.
                The Stewards determine that, albeit a breach technically occurred, the actions taken
                by the driver of Car 30 were appropriate given the circumstances and therefore do

No / Driver     11 - Sergio Perez
Competitor Cadillac Formula 1 Team
Time            16:11
Session         Qualifying
Fact            Car 11 was driving at reduced speed on the racing line through Turns 18, 19 and 20
                and forced Car 81 approaching in a flying lap to lift and change direction.
Infringement Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations and of item 27 of the Race
             Director’s Competition Notes (V2).
Decision        Drop of 3 grid positions for the next Sprint/Race in which the driver participates.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 11 (Sergio Perez), the driver of Car 81
                (Oscar Piastri), team representatives and reviewed video, timing, telemetry, team
                radio and in-car video evidence.
                PER was on a preparation lap between Turns 19 and 20 while PIA was approaching
                on a flying lap. PER had received two radio warnings that PIA was approaching. At
                the relevant point PIA was travelling at approximately 300 km/h, while PER was
                travelling at approximately 248 km/h.
                The Race Director’s specific traffic-management instructions required a driver on a
                preparation lap in this section of the circuit to remain on the right-hand side. PER was
                warming his tyres and, rather than maintaining a predictable line on the right-hand
                side, his tyre-warming manoeuvre placed him in the path of the approaching PIA. PIA
                consequently had to come off the throttle.
                PER explained that, in the circumstances, he considered that he had no other
                reasonable option. PIA confirmed that he had to lift because of PER, although he did
                not consider that he ultimately lost significant lap time as a consequence.
                The Stewards considered whether the incident was dangerous but, having reviewed
                the evidence and heard both drivers, determined that it was not. However, PER had
                received two warnings of PIA approaching and did not manage his preparation lap in
                accordance with the specific traffic-management instructions. The fact that PIA was
                required to lift was sufficient to establish that he had been unnecessarily impeded.
                The Stewards therefore determine that PER unnecessarily impeded PIA and apply
                the standard penalty for impeding during Qualifying.

No / Driver     44 - Lewis Hamilton
Competitor Scuderia Ferrari HP
Time            16:33

Fact            Impeding of car 30
Infringement Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations and of item 27 of the Race
             Director’s Competition Notes V2.
Decision        Driver: Reprimand (Driving).
                This is the driver’s 2nd reprimand of the season.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), the driver of Car 30
                (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed video, timing, telemetry, team
                radio and in-car video evidence.
                HAM was on an out lap and LAW was approaching on a flying lap. HAM had been
                informed twice by his team that LAW was approaching.
                The Race Director’s Competition Notes require cars on out laps or slow laps to
                remain on the extreme left from the exit of Turn 16 to the entry of Turn 18, and
                require Teams and Drivers to manage their gaps before Turn 18 so that they can
                travel from the apex of Turn 18 to the apex of Turn 19 without impeding a car on a
                competitive lap.
                HAM did not remain on the extreme left between Turns 16 and 18. Approaching Turn
                19, while LAW was closing from behind, HAM stayed on the racing line which required
                LAW to lift and slightly brake.The Stewards therefore determined that HAM did not
                follow the traffic-management instructions and unnecessarily impeded LAW.
                The normal penalty for an impeding infringement during Free Practice is a Warning
                unless it is dangerous or with intent. In this case, there was no intent but given the
                layout and the high speed corners as well as the specific instructions given by the
                Race Director, the impeding in the Stewards’ opinion was severe.
                The Stewards also took into account the difficulty to manage the energy deployment
                from Turn 16 to Turn 19 and the end of the lap. Additionally, both drivers mentioned
                during the hearing that when a driver has no more energy to deploy the difference of
                speed between the two cars in that specific section is important.
                Taking these circumstances into account, the Stewards impose a Driving Reprimand.

                The onboard video also showed that a yellow warning light was flashing on SAI’s
                steering wheel, indicating the yellow sector. SAI explained that in the circumstances
                he had not been able to pay attention to this warning.
                Approaching Turn 4, SAI braked slightly earlier than on the reference lap, but
                subsequently applied less brake pressure. At the exit of Turn 4 he accelerated more
                moderately than on the reference lap. Overall, he lost approximately 0.10 seconds in
                the relevant sector.
                From the exit of Turn 4 SAI was able to see the green light marking the end of the
                yellow sector. SAI acknowledged that, having seen the green light, he should have
                understood that he was still travelling within a yellow sector. Nevertheless, on the
                straight approaching the green light he accelerated up to the limiter while still within the
                yellow sector.
                The Stewards considered the fact that the Single Yellow was displayed only shortly
                before SAI entered Marshalling Sector 6 as a mitigating circumstance. However,
                taking into account the visible yellow indication, the warning displayed on the steering
                wheel, the telemetry and, in particular, SAI’s acceleration while still within the yellow
                sector after the green light had become visible, the Stewards were not satisfied that
                SAI had sufficiently reduced speed and exercised the required caution for a Single
                Yellow.
               The Stewards therefore determine that SAI failed to sufficiently reduce speed under
              the Single Yellow.
              The standard penalty under the Penalty Guidelines for such an infringement is a drop
              of 5 grid positions. However, the Stewards considered that there were mitigating
              circumstances, in particular the very short period between the Single Yellow being
              displayed and SAI entering the relevant marshalling sector. The Stewards also
              considered the penalties applied in comparable cases, where a Driving Reprimand
              has consistently been imposed in circumstances warranting mitigation from the
              standard penalty. The Stewards therefore considered a Driving Reprimand
              appropriate and consistent with those precedents.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 45) and
heard from the driver and team representative, have considered the following matter and determine
the following:

No / Driver     55 - Carlos Sainz
Competitor Atlassian Williams F1 Team
Time            17:03
Session         Qualifying
Fact            Failure to slow for yellow flags
Infringement Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 b) of the International Sporting Code
Decision        Drop of 5 grid positions for the next Sprint/Race in which the driver participates.
                2 penalty points (total of 4 for the 12 month period).
Reason          Reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 55 (Carlos Sainz), team
                representative and reviewed video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video
                evidence.
                Single Yellow Flags were displayed in Marshalling Sectors 4 and 5, in particular after
                Turn 2 and on the approach to Turn 3. The Yellow indications were clearly visible and
                SAI had also received a radio warning from the Team: “Yellow ahead, lift.” SAI
                confirmed at the hearing that he was aware of the Yellow Flag situation.
                SAI explained that he intended to demonstrate a reduction in speed across the Yellow
                area as a whole. He stated that he did not consider it necessary to reduce speed on
                the straight and instead intended to demonstrate his response when approaching and
                exiting Turn 3. He considered this to be a “global lift” covering the consecutive Yellow
                sectors. He further explained that the car which had originally caused the Yellow was
                no longer in the run-off area and that he expected the Yellow Flags to be withdrawn.
                The Stewards did not accept this interpretation. Where consecutive marshalling
                sectors are subject to Yellow Flag conditions, a driver must demonstrate a significant
                reaction to reduce speed in each individual Yellow marshalling sector. A reduction in a
                subsequent sector cannot retrospectively satisfy the requirement applicable to the
                preceding Yellow sector. The obligation is also not dependent on the driver’s own
                assessment of whether the original hazard remains present within a particular part of
                the Yellow sector.
                The telemetry clearly showed that SAI’s reaction to the Yellow occurred only in
                Marshalling Sector 5. There was no meaningful reduction in speed in Marshalling
                Sector 4 which could realistically be attributed to a response to the Yellow.
                Indeed, SAI recorded his fastest time of the session in Marshalling Sector 4.
               The Stewards therefore did not accept that the subsequent lift in Marshalling Sector 5
              constituted a sufficient “global” response covering both sectors. This is
              distinguishable from cases where the telemetry demonstrates a significant response
              to the Yellow even though the overall sector time reduction is relatively small.
              In the present case, SAI was aware of the Yellow, had received an explicit warning
              from the Team, the Yellow indications were clearly visible and the telemetry
              established that he did not demonstrate the required reaction in Marshalling Sector 4.
              The Stewards therefore determine that SAI failed to sufficiently reduce speed under
              the Single Yellow Flag in Marshalling Sector 4.
              The standard penalty under the Penalty Guidelines for this infringement during
              Qualifying is a drop of 5 grid positions.

TThe Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 60) and
heard from the driver and team representative, have considered the following matter and determine
the following:

No / Driver     5 - Gabriel Bortoleto
Competitor Audi Revolut F1 Team
Time            16:12
Session         Race
Fact            Overtaking under yellow flags
Infringement Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 b) of the International Sporting Code
Decision        10 second time penalty.
Reason          Reason: The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto), team
                representative and reviewed video and in-car video evidence.
                The incident occurred between Turns 6 and 7 during the first lap after the restart of
                the race. At the relevant time, marshal posts in this area were displaying physical
                “SC” boards together with waved Yellow Flags. However, the Stewards established
                that, at that time, the Safety Car had not in fact been deployed by Race Control.
                BOR explained that he initially reacted to the SC boards and Yellow Flags. However,
                he did not see any corresponding electronic indication and did not receive a Safety
                Car indication on his steering wheel. He was also informed by his Team that the
                Safety Car had not been deployed. BOR therefore became uncertain as to the actual
                status of the Race and, not wishing to lose position unnecessarily, subsequently
                overtook PER.
                The Stewards accept that the conflicting information contributed significantly to the
                situation. In particular, as the Safety Car had not been deployed, BOR cannot be
                considered to have overtaken another car under Safety Car conditions.
                However, this does not dispose of the separate issue of the waved Yellow Flags.
                BOR confirmed that he had seen the Yellow Flags but explained that, because they
                were displayed together with the SC boards, he understood them to be part of the
                same Safety Car indication and therefore considered that they were no longer
                relevant once he had been informed that the Safety Car had not been deployed.
                The Stewards do not accept this interpretation. A waved Yellow Flag is an instruction
                in its own right and must be respected irrespective of any accompanying signal. A
                driver cannot disregard a Yellow Flag based on his own assessment as to why it has
                been displayed or whether it should have been displayed. The 2026 FIA practice
                likewise treats Yellow Flag indications as requiring compliance even where
               surrounding circumstances are unusual.
              Accordingly, notwithstanding the understandable confusion concerning the SC
              boards, BOR had seen the waved Yellow Flags and nevertheless overtook PER while
              the Yellow Flag condition remained in effect. The Stewards therefore determine that
              BOR overtook another car under Yellow Flag conditions.
              The Stewards acknowledge that the erroneous SC indications and the conflicting
              information contributed to the circumstances of the incident. However, these
              circumstances do not remove the obligation to respect a waved Yellow Flag and the
              Stewards therefore apply the standard penalty for overtaking under a Single Yellow
              Flag.

Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 23 (Alexander Albon), the driver of Car 81
                (Oscar Piastri), the team representatives and reviewed video, in-car video and
                telemetry.

                following closely behind, to brake and take avoiding action. No collision or contact
                occurred.

                that he was below the required delta time and therefore reduced his speed in order to
                comply with the applicable delta requirement.
                PIA confirmed, having heard ALB's explanation, that he considered the reason for
                ALB's actions understandable.
                While the situation required a significant reaction from PIA and could potentially have
                developed into a dangerous situation, the Stewards were satisfied that ALB's actions
                were taken in an attempt to comply with the applicable delta requirements and
                explained the otherwise unusual reduction in speed at that location. His actions,
                therefore, did not constitute erratic or unnecessarily dangerous driving in the
                circumstances.
                Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that no
                infringement occurred and accordingly take no further action.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 54) and
heard from the driver and team representative, have considered the following matter and determine
the following:

No / Driver    1 - Lando Norris
Competitor McLaren Mastercard F1 Team
Time           18:08
Session        Race
Fact           Driving erratically under Safety Car conditions.
Infringement Breach of Articles B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations and Appendix L, Chapter IV,
             Articles 2 e) of the International Sporting Code.
Decision       Driver: Reprimand (Driving).
               This is the driver’s 1st reprimand of the season.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 1 (Lando Norris), the team representative
               and reviewed video and in-car video evidence.
               While following the Safety Car, NOR approached Turn 1 behind a group of cars. Car
               63 (George Russell) had stopped with a mechanical problem ahead of Turn 1, which
               caused the cars ahead of NOR to slow down. NOR explained that, due to the low sun
               and resulting visibility conditions, it was difficult to recognise that the cars ahead had
               started to slow earlier than would normally have been expected.
               NOR consequently misjudged his closing speed and approached the cars ahead too
               quickly. When he realised this, he braked heavily and deliberately steered to the left,
               onto the kerbs and then into the gravel bed in order to avoid contact with the cars
               ahead. By driving onto the kerbs, NOR had reduced grip available for braking, which
               further limited his ability to slow the car. In doing so, NOR momentarily overshot Car
               81 (Oscar Piastri), who was directly ahead of him.
               The Stewards considered whether this constituted an overtake while the Safety Car
               was deployed. Although NOR momentarily moved ahead of PIA, this occurred solely
               as a consequence of NOR leaving the track while taking avoiding action. PIA
               immediately repassed NOR while NOR was off the track. The Stewards therefore
               determined that this did not constitute an overtaking manoeuvre and take no further
               action in respect of this aspect of the incident.
               The Stewards also considered that, particularly while driving behind the Safety Car,
               NOR should have managed the gap to the cars ahead and his closing speed with
               greater care. The prevailing visibility conditions were circumstances which NOR
               should have taken into account when determining an appropriate speed and gap to
               the cars ahead, rather than a reason which excused the resulting driving. The need
              for heavy braking and an avoiding manoeuvre into the gravel demonstrated that NOR
              had not maintained an appropriate margin in the circumstances.
              The Stewards therefore determined that NOR had driven erratically in breach of
              Article B5.13.2a of the FIA F1 Regulations. Such a situation should not arise while
              driving behind the Safety Car, and NOR was required to maintain a sufficient margin
              to the cars ahead. However, taking into account that NOR reacted promptly once he
              recognised the situation and successfully avoided contact, the Stewards consider a
              Reprimand as appropriate.
              The Stewards separately considered NOR's return to the track. Although Car 18
              (Lance Stroll) was in relative close proximity, NOR returned progressively and without
              requiring STR to take avoiding action or otherwise creating an unsafe situation. The
              Stewards therefore determined that the re-join was safe.
              The Stewards also reviewed whether, after having re-joined the track, NOR had
              overtaken STR while the Safety Car was deployed. The video evidence showed that,
              as NOR returned from the gravel, he had already crossed the white line with at least
              one wheel and, as such, was back on track. At this point, he was ahead of STR and
              at no point did NOR pass STR. Rather, STR approached NOR while NOR was
              already in the process of returning to the track. The Stewards therefore determined
              that NOR had not overtaken STR under Safety Car conditions and as such also take
              no further action for this part of the incident.
              Accordingly, the Stewards impose a Reprimand on NOR for erratic driving. No further
              action is taken in relation to the re-join or the alleged overtake while the Safety Car
              was deployed.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 51) and
heard from the team representative, have considered the following matter and determine the
following:

No / Driver     27 - Nico Hulkenberg
Competitor Audi Revolut F1 Team
Time            17:35
Session         Race
Fact            Unsafe act during the pit stop resulting in an unsafe situation.
Infringement Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision        The competitor (Audi Revolut F1 Team) is fined €30,000 of which €20,000 is
                suspended for 12 months on condition that the Competitor does not commit a similar
                infringement during its pitstops in the meantime.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the team representative and reviewed video and in-car
                video evidence.
                During the pit stop of Car 27 (HUL), the automated release system initially displayed
                a green light after all four wheel guns had been removed from the wheel nuts and the
                respective mechanics had activated the release system.
                However, a mechanic was still in front of the car near the left-front wheel after having
                adjusted the front wing.
                The Team explained that its release procedure incorporates an additional manual
                safety check by a controller. When the responsible team member observed that the
                mechanic was still in front of the left-front wheel, the release signal was immediately
                changed back to red.
                HUL initially began to move away from the pit stop position in response to the green
                light. However, he immediately recognised that the light went back to red as the
                mechanic was still in front of the car and reacted promptly by stopping the car before
                it had fully left the pit stop position.
                The Stewards considered whether the initial green signal itself constituted an unsafe
                release. Article B1.6.2 defines when a car is deemed to have been released from its
                Designated Pit Stop Position. The relevant point is when the rear axle has passed the
                position previously occupied by the front axle while the car was stationary in its
                Designated Pit Stop Position.
                Accordingly, although the initial green signal was given prematurely and created an
                unsafe situation, the car was not “released” within the meaning of Article B1.6.2 while
                that situation existed. The Stewards therefore determine that no unsafe release
               occurred.
              In this case, although the initial green signal was given prematurely, the Team's
              backup safety procedure operated as intended and the signal was returned to red
              before the car had been released from its pit stop position. Nevertheless, the
              automatic premature green signal created an unsafe situation.
              While the Stewards determine that the circumstances did not constitute an unsafe
              release, the premature green signal nevertheless created an unsafe situation
              involving a team mechanic. The Stewards therefore impose a fine of €30,000 on the
              Competitor, of which €20,000 is suspended for the remainder of the 2026 season,
              subject to there being no further similar infringement. The substantial suspended
              element is intended to encourage the Competitor to review and, where necessary,
              improve its release procedures so as to prevent a recurrence of such an unsafe
              situation.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (documents 20 & 21)
and heard from the drivers and team representatives, have considered the following matter and
determine the following:

No / Driver     44 - Lewis Hamilton
Competitor Scuderia Ferrari HP
Time            16:24
Session         Free Practice 2
Fact            Car 44 unnecessarily impeded Car 5 on the entry to Turn 9.
Infringement Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        Driver: Warning.
                The competitor (Scuderia Ferrari HP) is fined €10,000.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 44 (Lewis Hamilton), the driver of Car 5
                (Gabriel Bortoleto), the team representatives and reviewed video, telemetry, team
                radio and in-car video evidence.
                HAM was travelling slowly approaching Turn 9 at approximately 80-85 km/h when
                BOR, who was on an out lap and not on a push lap, approached from behind at
                approximately 240 km/h, resulting in a closing speed of approximately 155-160 km/h.
                HAM moved from the middle of the track towards the racing line, at the end of the
                straight causing BOR to brake and take evasive action.
                The Stewards accept that HAM's right-hand mirror was damaged, as confirmed by
                photographic and video evidence, and that he had received no radio warning from the
                team. Both team representatives stated that such warnings are not normally issued
                where the approaching car is not on a push lap. BOR also confirmed that he
                remained in control of the situation.
                Nevertheless, the Stewards considered that HAM unnecessarily impeded the
                significantly faster approaching car by moving onto the racing line at slow speed. The
                fact that BOR was not on a push lap does not alter that conclusion.
                The Stewards also considered whether the incident should be regarded as dangerous
                impeding. In particular, they considered the high closing speed as well as the fact that
                a driver, who is aware that one of his mirrors is damaged, should exercise additional
                care before moving onto the racing line. However, BOR remained in control and was
                able to avoid HAM.
                The Stewards considered the damaged mirror and the fact that BOR was not on a
                push lap as mitigating circumstances. These were balanced against the significant
                speed differential, HAM's movement onto the racing line and the resulting need for
               BOR to take evasive action.
              Taking all the above into account, the Stewards determine that the standard penalty
              for impeding during a Practice session, which is a Warning, is appropriate.
              The Stewards also considered the responsibility of Scuderia Ferrari HP in relation to
              this incident.
              The Team was aware that HAM's right-hand mirror was damaged. As such, the
              Stewards determine that the Team should have provided appropriate radio warnings
              of significantly faster approaching cars, irrespective of whether those cars were on a
              push lap or not.
              The Stewards therefore determine that the Team failed to provide its driver with
              appropriate information in circumstances where it knew that his ability to observe
              approaching traffic was materially impaired by the damaged mirror and impose a fine
              of €10,000 on Scuderia Ferrari HP.

                lenient approach normally taken to “first-lap” (restart) incidents.

Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 14 (Stenshorne) allegedly impeded Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) between Turn 18-19
               in Qualifying 1.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 33 & 34) and heard the Drivers of Car 14
               (Stenshorne) and Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and the team representatives. They
               examined video and GPS evidence.
               Car 14 and Car 17 were preparing to start a push lap and this is done from the exit of
               Turn 16 on the preceding lap. Car 17 was behind Car 14 with an approximate 1
               second gap. Video evidence showed that Car 17 had closed the gap to Car 14 by
               Turn 19 and given that he had the benefit of a tow he had to slow. Car 17 then
               passed Car 14 and started his push lap. Car 14 abandoned the lap and entered the
               pit lane.
               The driver of Car 14 reported that he intended to start a push lap but when he saw
               that Car 17 had benefited from the tow and that he would likely be passed or would
               have to fight into Turn 1 he abandoned the lap.
               The driver of Car 17 reported that the preparation for a push lap starts at the exit of
               T16 and he expected Car 14 to be at full speed through T19 and T20 and he was
               surprised that Car 14 stayed on the line and appeared not to be at full speed. As a
               result of not having a tow on the main straight leading to the start of the push lap Car
               17 was 10 kph slower than he had been on previous laps when he had a car in front
               to give a tow.
               The only sector that could be affected by the interaction of Cars 14 and 17 on the
               push lap that started was Sector 1. In that sector Car 17 was 0.11 seconds slower
               than his fastest sector time which was achieved when he had the benefit of the tow.
               There is no doubt that Car 17 was affected by Car 14 who was not as fast through
               Turns 18 and 19 but that of itself is not evidence of unnecessary impeding. In fact
               Car 17 may have benefited from a tow from Car 14 up until Car 14 moved to the left
               to enter the pit lane. The Stewards therefore conclude that there is no evidence of
            unnecessary impeding and take no further action.

Reason         After the session, the Race Director reported a potential impeding incident involving
               Cars 5 and 17. The Stewards summoned (Documents 35 & 36) and heard the
               Drivers of Car 5 (Leon) and Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and the team representatives.
               They examined video, GPS and timing evidence.
               Car 17 was running behind Car 5 when both cars began a push lap. As they
               approached Turn 1, Cars 15 and 9 positioned ahead of Car 5 left the track, resulting
               in Car 5 effectively leading the pack through the subsequent corners. From that point
               onward, Car 17 steadily reduced the gap to Car 5, bringing it down to approximately
               one second by the approach to Turn 4.
               Both drivers continued pushing throughout the lap, with the driver of Car 17 opting to
               stay behind the car in front. At no point did Car 17 show a clear intention to overtake,
               and based on the available evidence, a pass was not achievable. The data showed
               that the driver of Car 5 achieved 2 of his fastest sectors in the early part of the lap
               but then he progressively lost time although still on a push lap.
               When assessing a potential impeding situation, the Stewards consider whether a
               driver has been unnecessarily impeded and whether the driver was affected. Having
               considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the driver of Car 17
               was affected but was not unnecessarily impeded by the driver of Car 5. Accordingly,
               no further action will be taken on this occasion.

Reason      The stewards received a report from the Race Director that Cars #7, 9, 6, 14, 20,
            5, 3, 2, 15, 16, 24, 17 were driving unnecessarily slowly between Turns 4 and
            7. After reviewing the video and telemetry the Stewards could see that all 12 cars
            involved were on the same sequence having just completed a push lap and were
            now on a cool down lap. Car 7 (the first car) slowed progressively without any
            sudden braking or change of direction and at all times remained off the racing line.

            As each driver behind caught up to Car 7 they also slowed and stayed in line
            without affecting any other driver. Eventually there was a line of 12 cars and at
            the exit of Turn 6 the entire pack of cars slowed to approximately 30 kph.
                                        BAKU EVENT

           The Stewards summoned and heard the drivers listed above and their team
           representatives, as well as the driver of Car 7 (Beganovic) and his team
           representative (Documents 37 to 48).

           The drivers each reported that they were aware that the following cars were all on
           the same sequence and were trying to stay in the order without passing They
           further reported that in their experience it is safer to stay in the sequence rather
           than pull out into the racing line and potentially end up impeding a following driver
           or driving side by side with another car. Eventually one of the cars at the rear of
           the pack did pull out and passed the line and the whole group accelerated without
           issue to Turns 7 and 8.

           Having considered the matter extensively and with special attention to recent
           similar incidents in this season the Stewards found that the conditions in this case
           were material different as there was no erratic driving, unusual braking and there
           did not appear to be any dangerous situation created. However, the driver of car
           7 did not need to slow to this level and still considered that the slow speed was
           unnecessary and in a separate decision issued a penalty. For the remaining
           drivers the Stewards elect to take no further action.

Competitor AIX Racing
Time           10:13
Session        Practice
Fact           Car 20 (Fittipaldi) overtook Car 3 (Miyata) under single yellow conditions between
               Turn 2 and Turn 3.
Infringement Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 20. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the
               2026 Season.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 14 & 16) and heard the Drivers of Car 20
               (Fittipaldi) and Car 3 (Miyata) and the team representatives. They examined video
               and GPS evidence.
               A car was stationary on track in T3 and this caused a single yellow to be displayed at
               panels 4 and 5. Panel 4 is at the exit of Turn 2 on the outside. Car 3 was on a cool
               down lap and was aware that Car 20 was on a push lap and approaching at high
               speed into Turn 2. Car 3 moved to the left off the racing line after exiting Turn 2. The
               driver of Car 20 explained that he was on a push lap and saw Car 3 ahead and was
               expecting to pass him after exiting Turn 2. He further explained that at the exit he
               saw Car 3 move to the left and he concentrated on avoiding him and still managing
               the exit of Turn 2.
               He noticed the panel ahead (panel 5) and immediately reduced speed. However, he
               admitted that by then he had passed Car 3 within the yellow flag sector which he had
               not seen.
               The Stewards find that Car 20 overtook Car 3 after passing Panel 4 while it was
               displaying a single-yellow signal. The driver’s failure to notice that signal does not
               remove the obligation to comply with it, and the Stewards therefore find a breach of
               Appendix H, Article 2.5.5(b).
               In determining the penalty, the Stewards took into account the relative speeds of the
               cars, Car 3’s movement off the racing line at the exit of Turn 2, the interaction
               between the cars at the start of the yellow-flag sector, and Car 20’s immediate
               reduction in speed upon observing Panel 5. Having considered the penalty
               recommended in the Penalty Guidelines for failing to slow under a single yellow as a
               comparator, the Stewards determine that a Driving Reprimand is proportionate to the
               particular circumstances of this overtaking infringement.

Fact           Car 7 (Beganovic) drove unnecessarily slowly in Qualifying 1 at 14:23 from Turn 4 to
               Turn 7.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (e) of the FIA International Sporting
             Code.
Decision       Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 7. This is his first Driving Reprimand of the
               2026 Season.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 37 to 48) and heard the Driver of Car 7
               (Beganovic) and his Team Representative, as well as the Drivers and Team
               Representatives of 11 additional cars (see Document 53). They examined video
               evidence.
               The Stewards received a report from the Race Director that Car 7 was driving
               unnecessarily slowly between Turns 4 and 7. After reviewing the video and telemetry
               the Stewards could see that all 12 cars involved were on the same sequence having
               just completed a push lap and were now on a cool down lap. Car 7 slowed
               progressively without any sudden braking or change of direction and at all times
               remained off the racing line.
               As each driver behind caught up to the growing pack, they also slowed and stayed in
               line without affecting any other driver. Eventually there was a line of 12 cars and at
               the exit of Turn 6 the driver of Car 7 slowed to approximately 30 kph.
               The driver reported that he was aware that the cars behind were on the same
               sequence and all would be doing a cool down lap. He reported that he slowed
               progressively and at all times remained off line and was aware of the cars behind him.
                He was anticipating that one of the cars would pass him such that he would no longer
               be at the head of the pack. Eventually one of the cars did so and then the entire group
               accelerated without incident.
               Having considered the matter extensively and with special attention to recent similar
               incidents in this season the Stewards found that the conditions in this case were
               materially different as there was no erratic driving, unusual braking and there did not
               appear to be any dangerous situation created. However, the Driver of Car 7 did not
               need to slow to this level and we still considered that the slow speed was
            unnecessary. Given the special circumstances we elect to issue a Driving
           Reprimand only.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    17 - Pedro Clerot
Competitor Rodin Motorsport
Time           10:38
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 6 (De Palo) and Car 17 (Clerot) collided at T1
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision       No Further Action
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 17 (CLE) attempted an outside
               overtake on Car 6 (DEP) at turn 1. CLE was ahead of DEP at the apex of turn 1 with
               approximately half of the car in front of DEP. As CLE turned in a collision occurred
               between the right-rear wheel of CLE and left-front wheel of DEP. DEP spun and lost
               several positions while CLE continued without any disadvantage. During the hearing,
               both drivers acknowledged that the other had respected their right to racing room and
               that the collision was a consequence of racing circumstances. Having considered the
               matter extensively, the Stewards determine that neither driver was wholly or
               predominantly responsible for the collision. Based on the totality of the
               circumstances, the Stewards elect to take no further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having decided to conduct a Right of Review (Document 42), have considered the
following matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    18 - Brando Badoer
Competitor Rodin Motorsport
Time           10:15
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 18 (Badoer) made nose to tail contact with Car 3 (Rivera) at turn 14 after Car 3
               experienced an electrical problem and loss of power.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision       In relation to the penalty applied to Car 18 in Document 30 we determine:
               a. The penalty is rescinded.
               b. The 10 seconds added to the elapsed race time of Car 18 on the provisional
               results shall be removed when preparing and issuing the final classification.
               c. The two (2) penalty points added to the driver’s record shall be removed. Total for
               the 2026 season = 0 points.
               d. No Further Action is taken in relation to the collision between Car 18 and Car 3 at
               Turn 14.
Reason         During the Sprint Race, the Stewards issued an in-race 10 seconds penalty to Car 18
               (BAD) for causing a collision with Car 3 (RIV). This penalty was issued during the
               session without a hearing based on the video evidence available. After the Sprint
               Race, the Team Manager of RIV informed the Stewards that RIV suffered an
               electrical failure on the exit of Turn 14 which caused it to lose power. The Stewards,
               having determined that this information constituted a significant, new and relevant
               element that was unavailable to them at the time of the decision, decided to re-
               examine Decision Document N. 30, pursuant Article 14.1.2 of the FIA International
               Sporting Code.
               The team representatives were summoned and heard. The Team Manager of RIV
               confirmed the technical failure which caused the loss of power of RIV at Turn 14 while
               BAD was approaching at full speed. The Team Manager of BAD stated that the driver
               had no time to react and to avoid RIV in front of him, who was losing power and
               speed.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that BAD was
               merely trying to avoid a stricken car, that he tried his best to avoid RIV, and that
               neither driver is wholly or predominantly responsible for the collision. Accordingly, the
               findings and penalties set forth in Document 30 are hereby vacated and revised as
              set forth herein.
              Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
              Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
              Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

No / Driver    11 - Maciej Gladysz
Competitor ART Grand Prix
Time           10:09
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 11 was out of position at the start of the race, taking the vacant position left by
               Car 7 which started in the pit lane.
Infringement Breach of Article 37.15 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Sporting
             Regulations.
Decision       A Drive-Through penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (c) of the FIA Formula 3
               Sporting Regulations. As the penalty was imposed after the race, it is converted to 20
               seconds added to the elapsed race time of the Driver concerned in accordance with
               Article 39.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. There are no penalty points
               associated with this infraction.
Reason         Car 7 started from the pit lane, causing its grid spot to be empty as other cars started
               to form up the grid. Car 11, which was supposed to start directly behind Car 7 in 17th
               position on the grid, moved up to Car 7’s spot, effectively having now started the race
               in 15th position. The Stewards consider that the advantage gained is significant
               enough to warrant an increased penalty for this type of infringement, and therefore
               consider the applied drive-through penalty appropriate and proportional.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 11 (Gladysz) impeded Car 28 (Barrichello) on the approach to Turn 10 during the
               Qualifying Session.
Infringement Breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       A drop of three grid positions for both races (Sprint and Feature Races) at this
               Competition. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
Reason         The Stewards examined video and GPS evidence They summoned and heard the
               drivers and team representatives (documents 16 & 17).
               Approaching Turn 10, Car 28 (BAR) was on a push lap. Car 11 (GLA), which had
               already aborted its lap, was driving slowly on the racing line at Turn 10.
               GLA explained that he saw BAR exceed track limits at Turn 9, that he thought that
               BAR was not pushing anymore, and that he did not expect his approach.
               Notwithstanding the fact that BAR exceeded track limits, the stewards determine that
               he was still entitled to push because he did not realize at the time that he had
               exceeded track limits. BAR was also entitled to keep pushing because the clock was
               running down and he had the chance to commence another push lap. GLA could have
               taken steps to avoid unnecessarily impeding BAR, but he did not do so. Accordingly,
               the Stewards apply the standard penalty for this infringement in a Qualifying session.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     22 - Nico Varrone
Competitor Van Amersfoort Racing
Time            14:49
Session         Race 1
Fact            Car 22 (Varrone) left the track at Turn 1 and gained lasting advantage over Car 11
                (Montoya).
Infringement Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision        Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2
                Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Documents 31 & 32) and heard the Drivers of Car 22
                (Varrone) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video
                evidence and onboard footage.
                During the hearing the Driver of Car 11 stated that he was ahead at the apex and he
                had the right of the corner. He also stated that at the apex, Car 22 moved slightly to
                the right, forcing him slightly to the kerb, which caused his car to snap, and contact
                with Car 22. That circumstance was confirmed by his team representative who added
                that the cars were alongside at the apex and it was not a dive in manoeuvre.
                The Driver of Car 22 stated that he was defending the position and he received a
                small contact due to a snap from Car 11 and, for that reason, Car 22 had to go off
                track and followed the escape road. The team representative of Car 22 also stated
                that his driver in this position could not have disappeared and it was the reason why
                he had to leave the track.
                The Stewards determined that the Drivers of Car 22 and Car 11 were fighting for
                position at Turn 1. Car 11 made an attempt to overtake and at the apex of Turn 1 was
                ahead of Car 22 that was defending the position. During the manoeuvre, Car 11 had
                a slight touch with Car 22 who at that moment lost the right of the turn. For the contact
                the Stewards found that no drivers were wholly or predominately to blame.
                However after the small contact, Car 22 went out of the track by using the escape
                road and in doing so gained the position on Car 11 when he rejoined the track. On
                this occasion, the Stewards consider that if a car defending the position leaves the
                track and re-joins in the same position, it has to be considered as having gained a
                lasting advantage.
                Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards noted that in this specific
                 case despite Car 22 trying to give some of the advantage back, the driver was unable
                to do it fully as Car 14 had overtaken Car 11. Therefore, the Stewards elected to
                assess a lower penalty than the baseline for such an offence.

                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

               didn’t brake earlier and/or noticeably reduce the speed in that sector as required by

No / Driver    6 - Matteo De Palo
Competitor Trident

Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 6 was out of position at the start of the race, taking the vacant position left by Car
               11.
Infringement Breach of Article 37.15 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Sporting
             Regulations.
Decision       A Drive-Through penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (c) of the FIA Formula 3
               Sporting Regulations. As the penalty was imposed after the race, it is converted to 20
               seconds added to the elapsed race time of the Driver concerned in accordance with
               Article 39.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. There are no penalty points
               associated with this infraction.
Reason         Car 7 started from the pit lane, causing its grid spot to be empty as other cars started
               to form up the grid. Car 11, which was supposed to start directly behind Car 7 in 17th
               position on the grid, moved up to Car 7’s spot. Car 6 followed Car 11’s movement
               and took up its space. This caused Car 6 to start from 17th position instead of the
               correct 19th position. The Stewards consider that the advantage gained is significant
               enough to warrant an increased penalty for this type of infringement, and therefore
               consider the applied drive-through penalty appropriate and proportional.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    6 - Nikola Tsolov
Competitor Campos Racing
Time           12:25
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 6 (Tsolov) went off track while passing Car 9 (Mini) and gained lasting
               advantage.
Infringement Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2
               Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 48 & 49) and heard the Drivers of Car 6
               (Tsolov) and Car 9 (Mini) and the team representatives. The Stewards, together with
               the Drivers and Team Representatives, reviewed video evidence including CCTV and
               drone footage, TV host high resolution images and Cars’ 6, 9, and 15 onboard
               cameras.
               The Driver of Car 6 explained that he was on soft tyres and he attacked Car 9 at the
               breaking point of Turn 10, where Car 9 ran wide. Due to the different tyre strategy, it
               was a simple move at the exit of Turn 10 and entry of Turn 11. He stated that he did
               not leave the track and that the move was already completed.
               The Driver Car 9 explained that he was defending the position, and that he exited turn
               10 quite tight leaving a lot of room at the inside of Turn 11 for Car 6. He also stated
               that Car 6 left the track and gained a lasting advantage by completing the manoeuvre
               off track.
               Having considered that matter extensively the Stewards determined that Car 6 left the
               track at Turn 11 and completed an overtaking move by exceeding the track limits.
               The Stewards find that mitigating circumstances exist to impose a 5 second time
               penalty on this occasion rather than the usual penalty of 10 seconds. The mitigating
               circumstances are that Car 6 left the track at Turn 11 for a extremely short period of
               time, video evidence also confirmed that despite Car 6 being off track, the distance to
               the white line was marginal, to the extent that the Stewards’ needed the TV host high
               resolution images to determine that an infringement was committed.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

  From       The FIA Formula 3 Stewards                           Document      42

The Stewards, having discovered that there may be a significant and relevant new element
unavailable to them at the time of the Decision (Document 30), rendered by them at the 2026
Barcelona Formula 3 Championship, decide the following on their own initiative in accordance
with Article 14.1.2 of the FIA International Sporting Code (ISC):

Facts:          During the Sprint Race, the Stewards issued an in-race penalty to Car 18 for
                causing a collision with Car 3. This penalty was issued without a hearing. After
                the Sprint Race, the Team Manager of Car 3 informed the Stewards that,
                moments before the collision with Car 18, Car 3 suffered an electrical failure on
                the exit of Turn 14 which caused it to lose power.

The Stewards, having received information from the team manager of Car 3, determine the
following:

Decision 1: The Stewards election to review the Decision is timely, proper, and valid.

Reasons:

         Deadline:       This decision is made within the deadline set forth in Article 14.4.1 of the
                         ISC.
         Deposit:        No deposit is required, in accordance with Article 14.4.3 of the ISC.

Decision 1 is subject to appeal in accordance with the applicable provisions of the ISC.

Decision 2: There is a significant and relevant new element which was unavailable to the
Stewards at the time of the decision in Document 30, no hearing having been conducted at
the time.


Reasons:

         1. Relevance

         The Stewards determine that the information provided by the Team Mangager of Car 3
         that the car was experiencing electrical problems and was losing power at the exit of
         turn 14 (the “Information”) relates directly to the collision at Turn 14 making it relevant.
                                   BARCELONA EVENT
                                      11 TO 14 JUNE 2026

       2. Significance
       The Information is of such a nature that it could cause the stewards to come to a new
       and different conclusion regarding fault for the collision, thus making the Information
       significant.

       3. New Element
       The Decision was made based exclusively upon video evidence. The Information was
       not previously known by the Stewards and is therefore new.

       4. Unavailable to the Stewards at the time of the Decision.
       The Stewards have neither live access to data from the car, nor in-race
       communication with the drivers or teams. Information about the operational condition
       of the car was unavailable to the Stewards at the time of the Decision.

Conclusion: The Stewards decide to re-examine the Decision pursuant to Article 14.1.2 of
the ISC.

Accordingly, a hearing will be conducted to re-examine the collision between Cars 3 and 18
at Turn 14.

Competitors are reminded that, in accordance with Article 14.3 of the ISC, Decision 2 is not
subject to appeal.
