No / Driver    5 - Noel Leon
Competitor Campos Racing
Time           14:57
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 5 (Leon) went off track at Turn 5 and gained lasting advantage over Car 24 (Van
               Hoepen).
Infringement Breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       Reprimand given to the Driver of Car 5 (Leon). This is his first Driving Reprimand of
               the 2026 Season.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 50 & 51) and heard the Drivers of Car 5
               (Leon) and Car 24 (Van Hoepen) and the team representatives. They
               examined video evidence.
               Car 24 made a pass on Car 5 going into Turn 5. Car 5 left the track, followed the RD
               instructions and took the correct path around the bollard but rejoined ahead of Car 24
               thereby gaining a position off track. After approximately 2.5 laps Car 5 gave back the
               position.
               At the hearing the driver of Car 5 explained that while he knew that he was passed on
               the inside of Turn 5 by Car 24 he was not sure if Car 24 had fully made the corner
               nor followed the RD instructions and as such was not sure if Car 24 was entitled to
               the position. He reported that he immediately asked his team to verify if Car 24 had
               made the corner and if so he would give back the position. The team had to wait for a
               replay to verify if the driver of Car 24 had in fact stayed on track. As soon as the
               team reported to him that Car 24 had remained on track he conceded the position.
               The Stewards also noted that Car 24 confirmed that the position had been fully
               restored and raised no further issue concerning the manner in which it was
               conceded. Although the position was ultimately conceded, the Stewards considered
               that retaining it for approximately 2.5 laps constituted a lasting advantage within the
               meaning of Article 27.3.
               The drivers have been trained that whenever they consider that they have gained a
               position off track they are to give back the position as soon as possible and at the
               latest within 1 lap. If in doubt it is always better to give up a position than to get a
               penalty after investigation. In this case the driver of Car 5 was fortunate that the
               position was still available to be given back after the lengthy delay of 2.5 laps. Given
               the unique circumstances in this case, and considering that the driver of Car 5 had
            immediately queried the status of Car 24 specifically if he had remained on track, the
           Stewards consider this significant mitigating circumstances that warrants a lesser
           penalty than the standard 10 seconds and gave a Driving Reprimand.
           Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
           Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
           Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Technical Delegate, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    10 - Taito Kato
Competitor ART Grand Prix
Time           21:12
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 10 (Kato) did not engage the required start set up procedure at the start of the
               Formation Lap for Feature Race 1
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 37.6 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       No further action
Reason         The Stewards, having received a report from the Technical Delegate (document 60),
               summoned the Driver and Team Representative (Document 61) and heard them
               along with the Technical Delegate and the Promoter’s Formula 3 Technical Director.
               During the hearing, the Driver of Car 10 (KAT) explained, and the Technical Delegate
               confirmed, that KAT had successfully engaged the start set-up procedure before
               initially attempting to start the car. KAT experienced technical difficulties and was
               unable to start the car. The master power had to be reset before the car would start.
               The Technical Delegate confirmed that after the reset, KAT properly attempted to
               engage the start set-up procedure three times before the car was started.
               Nevertheless, the procedure was not successfully engaged. The F3 Technical
               Director confirmed that the issue was with the Car itself, and that it was not
               attributable to the Team.
               KAT commenced the formation lap without the start set-up procedure engaged.
               However, he was able to successfully engage it for the Race start as required by
               Article 37.9 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. Having considered the matter
               extensively, the Stewards determine that neither KAT nor his Team were responsible
               for the issue, and that KAT made all reasonable efforts to engage the start set-up
               procedure. Taking all the mitigating circumstances into consideration, the Stewards
               elect to take No Further Action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    22 - Jose Garfias
Competitor PREMA Racing
Time           10:24
Session        Race 3
Fact           Car 4 (Stromsted) and Car 22 (Garfias) collided at Turn 2.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the
               Drivers and Team Representatives (documents 73 and 74).
               Car 22 (GAR) was attempting an inside pass of Car 4 (STR) at T1 and had properly
               established his rights to the corner since he was slightly ahead at the apex. GAR did
               not make a full exit at Turn 1 which leads directly into the second part of the chicane.
                This allowed STR to remain on track and maintain partial overlap with GAR
               approaching Turn 2. STR ran out of room at the apex of Turn 2 where the cars
               collided causing GAR to spin. Generally, in chicanes, the car that established its
               rights in the first corner has the rights to the entire segment; however, it remains
               possible for the car that lost the rights to the first corner to reestablish its rights in the
               second corner.
               Once GAR allowed STR to remain on track after Turn 1, STR was entitled to fight
               back at Turn 2, and he did. Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards
               determine that even though GAR had the initial rights to the chicane, under the
               circumstances, STR had the right to contest Turn 2. Even though GAR remained
               ahead on the outside of Turn 2, he could not reasonably expect STR to disappear
               and he could have allowed STR more racing room on the inside of Turn 2. Having
               lost the rights at T1, STR could have declined to push the position, and GAR, having
               allowed STR to remain on track, could have allowed him more room at Turn 2. The
               Stewards determine that neither driver is wholly or predominantly at fault for the
               collision. Given that both drivers could have taken steps to avoid the collision, the
               Stewards elect to take no further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Reason          The Stewards examined video & GPS evidence.

                that if a car leaves the track while defending a position and re-joins retaining the
                position, that it has gained an advantage. In this circumstance EDE would be

                extensively, the Stewards determine that EDE gained a lasting advantage and elect to
                impose the standard penalty for such an infraction.

Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. The Stewards summoned and heard the

               seconds just after his car’s nose entered the fast lane. After a few moments SHI
               slowly entered the pit lane and YAM came to a complete stop to avoid him.
               During the hearing SHI explained that he had been experiencing clutch issues and
               that is why he stopped. Video showed his mechanic leaning over the cockpit to attend
               to him, and SHI then departing on his own. YAM explained that he could see the
               situation unfolding and that he had reasonable time to react. Nevertheless, the
               Stewards determine that once SHI stopped, the mechanic could have taken better
               steps to re-establish release control over the car. Under the circumstances, the
               Stewards determine that a warning to the team is appropriate for this pre-race
               infringement.

               performed with Car 7 (Colnaghi) directly in front of him on the grid.
Infringement Breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the FIA International Sporting Code - failure to follow
             Competition Notes, Item 15.1.b).
Decision       Warning
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and
               team representative (document 17).
               DEP explained that he released the clutch when Car 7 (COL) first
               moved. Unfortunately, COL immediately stalled and became stationary. DEP then
               moved immediately into the center lane and passed COL. Item 15.1.b of the
               Competition Notes provides that, “Under no circumstances should a driver make a
               practice start if another car is still stationary ahead on the same side of the grid.”
               The stewards acknowledge that COL’s stall played a factor in the situation, that DEP
               tempered his practice start once he realized that COL had stalled and that the
               passing manouevre did not prove to be dangerous to any other cars. The Stewards
               determine that a practice start infringement occurred, but in light of the forgoing
               mitigating circumstances elect to issue a warning which is less than the standard
               penalty for such an infraction.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following

No / Driver    11 - Sebastian Montoya

Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 11 (Montoya) was alleged to have failed to follow the Race Director Competition
               Notes (Document 6) and returned to the F1 pit lane instead of the F2 pit lane.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.i of the 2026 FIA International Sporting Code
             - Failure to follow the instructions of the relevant officials for the safe and orderly
             conduct of the Event.
             Item 25.2 of the Race Director’s Competition Notes - General Instructions and
             Information - At the end of the qualifying session all cars must continue after taking
             the chequered flag, and leave the track via the Support Pit Lane, proceeding directly
             to Parc Fermé. Drivers must follow marshals’ instructions.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Document 21) and heard the Driver of Car 11 (Montoya)
               and the team representative. They examined video evidence.

               qualifying session but explained that he intended to enter the support pit lane but, as
               he was doing so, he saw a marshal standing in the pit lane pointing towards the
               Formula 1 Pit Lane and understood this to be a direction not to enter the support pit
               lane but to enter the Formula 1 pit lane and did so.
               The Stewards reviewed the available footage from the car, which confirms the
               driver’s version and accept that is a reasonable excuse for the driver not to follow the
               Race Director’s instructions for the end of the qualifying session and take no further

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     22 - Nico Varrone
Competitor Van Amersfoort Racing
Time            14:59
Session         Race 1
Fact            Incident between Car 22 (Varrone) in the fast lane and Car 21 (Shields) waiting to
                depart his pit box.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 5 (b) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Documents 40 & 41) and heard the Drivers of Car 22
                (Varrone) and Car 21 (Shields) and the team representatives. The Stewards
                reviewed the available evidence, including video footage from the pit lane cameras.
                During the Safety Car period, Car 22 entered the pit lane to perform a tyre change.
                The team of Car 22 was conducting a double-stacked pit stop. When Car 22 was
                approaching its pit position, its team-mate was still stationary due to a problem during
                the pit stop and could therefore not be released in time.
                At the same time, Car 21, which was pitted in the pit position behind Car 22, was
                ready to be released. However, the team of Car 21 acted conservatively and delayed
                the release of Car 21 in order to avoid a potential unsafe release into the fast lane
                with Car 22.
                As the driver of Car 22 did not want to stop in the fast lane, he proceeded forward in
                the pit lane and moved ahead of Car 21. Only after Car 22 had cleared the area was
                Car 21 able to leave its pit position.
                The Stewards acknowledge that Car 21 was impeded as a result of this situation.
                However, having considered the circumstances, the Stewards determined that Car
                22 did not stop in the fast lane and did not perform any manoeuvre considered
                dangerous or in breach of the pit lane regulations. The situation arose as a
                consequence of the delayed release of Car 22’s team-mate during the double-stack
                pit stop and the cautious release decision taken by the team of Car 21.
                Accordingly, the Stewards find no breach of the Regulations and therefore take no
                further action.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
            Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    20 - Louis Sharp
Competitor PREMA Racing
Time           11:31
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 20 (Sharp) collided with Car 21 (Wharton) at Turn 5.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       Ten second (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3
               Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for
               the 2026 season = 2 points.
Reason         The stewards examined video and telemetry evidence. Having considered the matter
               extensively, the stewards determine Cars 20 (SHA) and 21 (WHA) had been racing
               hard since Turn 1 with WHA leading. They got side by side in Turn 3 and SHA
               attempted an outside pass on (WHA) at Turn 4. SHA was not ahead at the apex and
               had not earned the right to be given room on the exit. WHA properly made a full exit
               which caused SHA to exceed track limits on the exit. The stewards accept that SHA
               could not simply disappear even though he was obliged to concede the corner. At this
               point, SHA was required to rejoin safely and without gaining a lasting advantage.
               Telemetry indicated that SHA maintained full throttle in the runoff area which put him
               in position to set up for an inside pass at Turn 5. Being in position to attack, when he
               should have properly conceded, constituted an advantage to which SHA was not
               entitled.
               WHA turned into Turn 5 and collided with SHA who was midway alongside.
               Regardless of the question of gaining an advantage, SHA had not established
               sufficient position to have gained the right to racing room on the inside. The stewards
               determine that SHA is wholly responsible for the collision and elect to apply the
               standard penalty.

               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    10 - Pierre Gasly
Competitor BWT Alpine F1 Team
Time           16:12
Session        Race
Fact           The driver left the track at turn 1 and rejoined after turn 3, gave a position back to car
               43, then at the end of the straight after turn 3, he was passed by car 30 at turn 4.
               Minor contact occurred during that passing manoeuvre.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video and in-car video
               evidence.
               Although the additional guidelines issued by the Stewards on October 31 advised that
               a car leaving the track at turn 1 after a Restart should yield the position by Turn 4, the
               fact that the correct positions were achieved by turn 5 confirms to the Stewards that
               no further action is required. In leaving the track Car 10 did not gain a position, in fact
               the car ultimately lost a position to car 30.
               The minor contact between the cars does not require penalization to either driver.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

               Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely
               on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

No / Driver     6 - Isack Hadjar
Competitor Oracle Red Bull Racing
Time            12:20
Session         Free Practice 1
Fact            The driver and a Paddock guest appeared to have an interaction in the Paddock prior
                to the start of FP1.
Infringement Breach of Article 12.2.1.l of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision        Driver: Formal warning.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 6 (Isack Hadjar) and the
                team representative and reviewed video evidence.
                The driver stated that he was running late for FP1 and had stopped to have a
                photograph with a young fan, when he was approached by a Paddock guest in an
                aggressive manner. One security person was walking behind him and was unable to
                intervene and prevent what was tantamount to an invasion of the driver’s private
                space. The driver initially resisted the move by placing his hand on the waist of the
                guest, holding him at bay, then the driver pushed him aside with his open right hand.
                This latter action by the driver is regarded as a breach of the regulations however in
                mitigation of penalty the stewards considered the following matters (in accordance
                with the guidelines provided in Appendix B of the FIA International Sporting Code):

                a) The driver was reacting to an uninvited and rather aggressive action by another
                person
                b) The driver was endeavouring to make his way to the start of FP1 through a
                congested area

determine the following:

No / Driver    81 - Oscar Piastri
Competitor McLaren Mastercard F1 Team
Time           16:04
Session        Race
Fact           Car 81 collided with Car 41 at the entry to turn 2
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       10 second time penalty imposed after the Race.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 81 (Oscar Piastri), the driver of Car 41
               (Arvid Lindblad), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system
               data, video and in-car video evidence.
               On the approach to turn 1 the driver of Car 81 attempted an overtake on the outside
               of Car 41. Car 81 was never fully alongside Car 41 so was not able to claim the right
               to the corner. Through turn 1, the driver of Car 41 defended his position by releasing
               the brakes however does not force Car 81 off the track, allowing racing room on the
               outside – which he is not required to do.
               The Stewards determined that the collision could have been avoided if the driver of
               Car 81 had moved further to the left after turn 1, even if this involved leaving the track
               prior to turn 2.

Fact            During the feature race Car 24 was released from its pit box ahead of Car 22.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision        No further action
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Documents 58 and 59) and heard the Driver and team
                representative of Car 3 and Car 12 and reviewed video evidence.
                The driver of car 24 reported that he left his pit position as soon as he was signaled
                to do so. He said he saw that there were no cars in the fast lane behind. He said
                that he had some wheel spin from the wet conditions but upon entering the fast lane
                he saw that car 22 was now fully in the fast lane, and decided that it was safer to
                continue than to brake.
                The driver of car 22 reported that he saw car 24 entering ahead and had to lift and
                tap his brakes a little.
                The stewards considered the evidence and determined that the fast lane was indeed
                still empty when car 24 was released, car 22 having been released only a moment
                before and still accelerating to the pit lane speed as car 24 entered. Although the
                cars ended up in close proximity, it did not reach the threshold of being unsafe in the
                conditions and under these particular circumstances. It appeared that both drivers
                acted appropriately and no rule was breached.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

  To        The Team Manager, PREMA Racing                        Date           7 May 2026

                         Decision: Right of Review Withdrawal
Timeline
Petition for Review received: 5 May 2026 / 07:25 EDT
Acknowledgement of receipt issued by the Stewards: 5 May 2026 / 10:23 EDT
Notice of withdrawal received from PREMA Racing: 5 May 2026 / 13:29 EDT
Acknowledgement of withdrawal issued by the Stewards: 6 May 2026 / 09:59 EDT


Background

The Stewards received from PREMA Racing, in writing, a petition pursuant to Article 14 of the FIA
International Sporting Code seeking review of Decision Document 74, rendered by the Stewards at
the 2026 Miami Event, concerning the alleged unsafe release of Car 3 into the path of Car 12 during
the Feature Race.
The petition was received within the 96-hour deadline prescribed by Article 14.4.1 of the FIA
International Sporting Code, and was accompanied by the prescribed deposit of €2,000.
PREMA Racing subsequently informed the Stewards in writing that it wished to withdraw the petition
for review.


Decision


   1. The petition for review submitted by PREMA Racing in respect of Decision Document 74 is
      treated as withdrawn. The Stewards make no determination under Article 14.1.1 of the FIA
      International Sporting Code as to whether the petition disclosed a significant and relevant
      new element.
   2. Of the deposit of €2,000 lodged in respect of the petition, €1,000 is retained and €1,000 is
      returned to PREMA Racing.
   3. Decision Document 74 is unaffected by the present Decision and stands as issued.


Reason

The FIA International Sporting Code does not prescribe a specific procedure for the withdrawal of
a petition for review submitted under Article 14. Acting in their procedural authority over the matter,
the Stewards accept the withdrawal of the petition by PREMA Racing and conduct no further
proceedings in respect of it.
                                         MIAMI EVENT
                                    30 APRIL TO 3 MAY 2026

Article 14.4.3 of the Code provides that the deposit accompanying a petition for review "may only
be returned if the right of review is upheld, unless fairness requires otherwise." The default position
under the Code is therefore that the deposit is retained where the right of review has not been
upheld. The right of review has not been upheld in this matter, no determination under Article 14.1.1
having been made.
The Stewards have considered whether the fairness proviso in Article 14.4.3 displaces the default
in this case, and conclude that a partial return is appropriate having regard to the following case-
specific factors:
   (i) PREMA Racing’s notice of withdrawal was communicated to the Stewards before any
   substantive consideration of the merits of the petition, sparing the procedural and time costs of
   a hearing;
   (ii) The petition had been filed in proper form, within the 96-hour deadline prescribed by Article
   14.4.1 of the Code, and accompanied by the prescribed deposit; and
   (iii) The Code’s silence on the procedure for withdrawal of a petition for review weighs in favour
   of a measured rather than absolute outcome on the deposit, given the absence of any explicit
   textual guide for the present situation.
The Stewards have exercised the fairness proviso in Article 14.4.3 on the particular facts of this
petition; this exercise of discretion is specific to this matter and does not establish, and is not
intended to establish, any precedent. Competitors and Teams competing in the FIA Formula 2
Championship are accordingly placed on notice that the default position under Article 14.4.3 — that
the deposit is retained where the right of review is not upheld — will be strictly applied to future
petitions. Future petitions for review that are not upheld, whether through withdrawal,
inadmissibility, or failure of the significant-and-relevant-new-element test under Article 14.1.1,
should expect that the deposit will be retained per that regulatory default. The fairness proviso will
not be exercised lightly.
In accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code, the rights of appeal from the
present Decision are governed by that Article and the procedural rules set out in Chapter 5 of the
Judicial and Disciplinary Rules.

Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 10 (Goethe) crossed the white line at pit entry.
Infringement Breach of ISC Apdx L Chap IV (d)
Decision       Warning to driver
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and
               team representative (document 55).
               At the start of the race Lap 1 Turn 1 an incident occurred necessitating the
               deployment of the Safety Car. As the leaders were approaching T17 the Race
               Director notified the teams that the drivers should follow Safety Car through the pit
               lane. Panels 19 and 20 were illuminated with a yellow arrow pointing to the right.
                The RD used this signal per Art 40.11 with the intention of notifying the drivers to
               enter the pit lane. The leader was approximately 50 meters before panel 19 when it
               was illuminated.
               The track condition was very wet and there was significant spray reducing visibility
               although it appeared from the drivers onboard camera that the panels were visible.
                There is no way for the Stewards to know when the drivers were notified by radio of
               the RD’s instruction to enter the pit lane. Some teams may react quicker than others
               and it is impossible to know what other radio traffic may affect how quickly the
               message can be delivered to individual drivers.
               The light panel signal showing a red arrow on a yellow background is used to indicate
               to a driver the side of the track that they should chose because of an issue in the
               area. It is not an exclusive instruction to enter the pit lane. The RD Competition
               Notes does not specifically state that when panels 19 and 20 are illuminated in this
               way that drivers are to enter the pit lane.
               Car 10 (Goethe) entered the pit entry road after the bollard at SC1 crossing the solid
               white line in breach of ISC Apex L Ch IV (d).
               The driver explained that he got the call very late from his engineer and up to that time
               had only understood that the signals on panel 19 and 20 were for him to stay to the
               right. Once he had a clear instruction to enter the pit lane he determined that it would
               be more safe to ignore the white line and do as instructed as opposed to staying out.
            While the driver contravened Apdx L he did prioritize safety and followed the Race
           Directors instruction as he understood it. No driver benefited nor was harmed by this
           action. When racing was resumed after the safety car period all drivers were in the
           correct positions with no advantage gained.
           Consequently the Stewards decide that while the regulations were breached the
           appropriate penalty in this case is a Warning to the driver given the late call and the
           lack of clarity surrounding the instructions.

               rejoined at Turn 12 gaining a position over Car 4. A successful overtake requires the
               driver to complete the manoeuvre on track.

               The drivers were informed by the FIA Race Director during the Drivers Meeting that

               circumstances that no yellow flag was shown nor light panel was illuminated and the
               facts of the configuration of this new circuit and the short time between the last car
               that had not seen the chequered flag and the first car that crossed the line after the
               session finished was very short and as such the marshals could not be on track and
               waving the flag. However, it is responsibility of the driver to follow the RD instructions
               and he did not.

               mentioned above, the Stewards elect to give a warning to the driver.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    9 - Gabriele Mini
Competitor MP Motorsport
Time           09:41
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 9 (Mini) crossed the white line at pit entry.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 4 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       Warning to driver
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the driver and
               team representative (document 62).
               At the start of the race Lap 1 Turn 1 an incident occurred necessitating the
               deployment of the Safety Car. As the leaders were approaching T17 the Race
               Director notified the teams that the drivers should follow Safety Car through the pit
               lane. Panels 19 and 20 were illuminated with a yellow arrow pointing to the right.
                The RD used this signal per Art 40.11 with the intention of notifying the drivers to
               enter the pit lane. The leader was approximately 50 meters before panel 19 when it
               was illuminated.
               The track condition was very wet and there was significant spray reducing visibility
               although it appeared from the drivers onboard camera that the panels were visible.
                There is no way for the Stewards to know when the drivers were notified by radio of
               the RD’s instruction to enter the pit lane. Some teams may react quicker than others
               and it is impossible to know what other radio traffic may affect how quickly the
               message can be delivered to individual drivers.
               The light panel signal showing a red arrow on a yellow background is used to indicate
               to a driver the side of the track that they should chose because of an issue in the
               area. It is not an exclusive instruction to enter the pit lane. The RD Competition
               Notes does not specifically state that when panels 19 and 20 are illuminated in this
               way that drivers are to enter the pit lane.
               Car 9 (Mini) entered the pit entry road after the bollard at SC1 crossing the solid white
               line in breach of ISC Apex L Ch IV (d).
               The driver explained that he got the call very late from his engineer and up to that time
               had only understood that the signals on panel 19 and 20 were for him to stay to the
               right. Once he had a clear instruction to enter the pit lane he determined that it would
               be more safe to ignore the white line and do as instructed as opposed to staying out.
            While the driver contravened Apdx L he did prioritize safety and followed the Race
           Directors instruction as he understood it. No driver benefited nor was harmed by this
           action. When racing was resumed after the safety car period all drivers were in the
           correct positions with no advantage gained.
           Consequently the Stewards decide that while the regulations were breached the
           appropriate penalty in this case is a Warning to the driver given the late call and the
           lack of clarity surrounding the instructions.
           Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
           Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
           Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (documents 81 & 82)

determine the following:

No / Driver     30 - Liam Lawson
Competitor Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
Time            13:12
Session         Race
Fact            Collision between cars 30 and 10 in Turn 17.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), the driver of Car 10
                (Pierre Gasly), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system
                data, video, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence.
                Car 10 (Pierre Gasly), was attempting an outside pass of Car 30 (Liam Lawson) at
                the entry to Turn 17. Car 10 was clearly ahead prior to the apex and had established
                its rights under the Driving Standards Guidelines. A significant collision occurred and
                Car 10 was pushed into the barriers, with the car flipping and ending up wedged in the
                TechPro.
                The driver of Car 30 explained that just before the collision, he had a technical issue
                as his gearbox failed under braking. The Stewards reviewed the in-car data and
                telemetry and confirmed that there was clearly a gearbox failure just before the
                incident in question. The radio communications were also consistent with the fact that
                there was a gearbox failure.
                We therefore accept the driver’s explanation that this was a failure of a mechanical
                part in the car and that there was nothing that he could do to avoid the collision.
                We also considered whether the driver of Car 30 had the ability to anticipate the
                failure of the gearbox and decided that it would not have been possible for him to do
                so.
                Under the circumstances, the stewards determine that a mechanical failure, not
                driver error, was the cause of the collision and therefore the driver of Car 30, was not
                at fault for the collision. We therefore took no further action.

Session         Sprint
Fact            Engine intake air pressure exceeded maximum permitted limit.
Infringement Breach of Article C5.3.2 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        Car 5 is disqualified from the Sprint classifications.
Reason          The Stewards reviewed the report received from the Technical Delegate and found
                that the requirement was for the engine intake air pressure to be less than 4.8 barA at
                all times. The pressure was measured by two FIA approved devices that were
                installed in FIA approved locations situated in the engine intake air system
                downstream of the charge air cooling system.
                The Stewards heard from the team representatives of Car 5. They admitted that the
                Technical Delegate’s finding was correct. However, in mitigation, they explained that
                this happened over one lap, when the temperatures rose higher than they had
                expected. As soon as that became apparent, they took steps to bring the pressure
                back in line with the regulations. While the fact that they took steps to bring the car
                back in compliance is recognized, the regulations make it clear that the car needs to
                be in compliance ‘at all times’, which it was not.
                Given that this is a technical infringement, the usual penalty of a disqualification of
                Car 5 from the Sprint classification was applied.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    11 - Maciej Gladysz
Competitor ART Grand Prix
Time           07:50
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 8 (Taponen) and Car 11 (Gladysz) collided at Turn 18.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence.
               Car 11 (GLA) was attempting an inside overtake on Car 11 (TAP) at turn 18. TAP
               turned in earlier than normal as part of his defense thus squeezing GLA while still
               leaving him racing room. GLA did not have his front axle alongside TAP’s mirror prior
               to the apex which means that he had not won the corner. While this would ordinarily
               mean that he was responsible for any ensuing collision, the stewards determine that
               TAP’s defensive move was made late enough that he contributed to the collision.
               Under the circumstances, the Stewards do not find either driver to be wholly or
               predominantly responsible for the collision. Based on the totality of the
               circumstances, the Stewards elect to take no further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact            Car 24 (van Hoepen) was alleged to have been the sole cause of the issue of the red
                flag in Qualifying, after contact from Car 16 (Maini).
Infringement Breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision        No further action. As a result of the contact, Car 24 was outside the 107% for the
                qualifying time. Permission is given for Car 24 to start Race 1 (Sprint) and Race 2

Reason          The Stewards summoned (Documents 27 & 28) and heard the Drivers of Car 24
                (Van Hoepen) and Car 16 (Maini) and the team representatives. They examined
                video evidence.

                collided with Car 24 at Turn 10. As a result of the collision, Car 24 to spun and
                became stranded on the kerb at Turn 10. The Race Director red flagged the session
                due to this incident. Having considered the matter extensively and consulted with the
                Race Director, the Stewards determined that no car was the sole cause of the red
                flag. Accordingly, the Stewards decided that no further action is required.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Technical Delegate, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     14 - Hiyu Yamakoshi
Competitor Van Amersfoort Racing
Time            17:56
Session         Race 1
Fact            The front push rod LH - CPL (part number: F32506D001) of car #14 was mounted on
                the right-hand side of the car and the front push rod RH - CPL (part number:
                F32506D002) was mounted on the left-hand side of the car.
Infringement Breach of Articles 1.5.3 and 17.1 of the FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
Decision        Car 14 is disqualified from the Sprint Race classification. All other drivers move up in
                the classification.
Reason          The Stewards summoned and heard the driver and team representative (document
                61) and the FIA Formula 3 Technical Delegate.
                During the hearing the team representative acknowledged that the facts as stated
                above are true and correct: specifically, that the front push rod LH - CPL (part
                number: F32506D001) of car #14 was mounted on the right-hand side of the car and
                the front push rod RH - CPL (part number: F32506D002) was mounted on the left-
                hand side of the car.
                The team representative disputed that these facts constitute a breach of the FIA
                Formula 3 Technical Regulations. (For the sake of convenience any and all Article
                references hereinafter contained are with respect to the FIA Formula 3 Technical
                Regulations.)
                While the Technical Delegate’s report included a reference to Article 1.5.2, it is not
                alleged that the parts in question were modified. They were not. The question at hand
                is whether the parts were installed on the wrong side of the car.
                The FIA Technical Delegate and the team representative both referred to the
                language of Article Article 1.5.3 and Article 17.1 The relevant part of Article 1.5.3
                provides, “For the avoidance of doubt the original design and construction of the car
                must be maintained at all times.” Article 17.1 titled General Principles begins, “The
                complete car is divided into three types of parts. The parts are classified in the spare
                parts catalogue.”
                The stewards find that the “original design and construction of the car” is illuminated
                by Article 17.1. It is clear that the car is made up of parts and that the parts are
                specified in the spare parts catalogue.
               The front pushrod is depicted on page 006D of the spare parts catalogue which also
              includes line references to “front push rod LH – CPL” (part number: F32506D001)
              and “front push rod RH – CPL” (part number: F32506D002) are listed on page 006G
              of the catalogue.
              The Technical Delegate explained that the front push rod LH is meant to be installed
              on the left hand side of the car, and vice versa. The team’s contention is that “LH”
              and “RH” are not defined within the spare parts catalogue as “left side” and “right
              side” and that, in the absence of a formal definition, the matter is unclear, vague and
              easily subject to misinterpretation. Given the alleged ambiguity, they feel that the car
              is compliant notwithstanding the facts of the installation.
              The stewards acknowledge that references to left or right with respect to a race car
              are taken to mean left or right from the driver’s point of view. Having considered the
              matter extensively, the stewards determine that the abbreviations LH and RH, which
              are used extensively throughout the catalogue, and are so commonplace within the
              world at large as to not reasonably require express definition within the sophisticated
              world of Formula 3. Furthermore, if the team had any confusion about what the
              abbreviations meant they had ample opportunity to seek clarification from the
              Technical Delegate and they did not do so.
              The stewards also note that the lower front wishbones (part number: F32506G001
              and F32506G002) to which these parts connect are also designated and labeled as
              LH and RH. The Technical Delegate confirmed that the wishbones were correctly
              installed on the expected left hand and right hand sides of the car. In this case, the
              team connected front pushrod LH to front lower wishbone RH, and vice versa.
              The team points out that regardless of a parts name, many part's can only
              successfully be installed on one side of the car. While that may be true, the stewards
              believe that even in face of alleged ambiguity or confusion, the team ought to notice
              that the parts that wind up on the right hand side of the car are designated RH, and
              that the parts that wind up on the left hand side of the car are designated
              LH. Accordingly, the stewards further determine the meaning of LH and RH should be
              clear to the team based on its overall experience with the car and its numerous parts
              over time.
              The stewards determine that the front push rod LH – CPL must be installed on the left
              hand side of the car and that the front push rod RH – CPL must be installed on the
              right hand side of the car. The stewards determine that Articles 1.5.3 and 17.1 of
              FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations have therefore been breached and that the
              standard penalty of a disqualification needs to be applied for such an infringement.
              Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
              Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
              Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Time            15:11
Session         Qualifying
Fact            A team member momentarily entered the Fast Lane to release Car 7.
Infringement Breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code - potentially unsafe
             act.
Decision        Reprimand to the Team.
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Document 32) and heard the Team representative. They
                examined video evidence.
                During the qualifying session, a team member momentarily entered the fast lane to
                release Car 7. For safety reasons, it is essential that team members avoid crossing
                the white line separating the blending lane from the fast lane. This rule is crucial for
                maintaining safety and minimizing risks during high-pressure moments on the pit
                lane.
                The team manager explained that the limited space provided by the F1 Teams
                prevented them from having the necessary room to operate effectively. This was
                confirmed by the Race Director, who explained that a request would be made to
                improve this for all remaining sessions.
                Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards concluded that, although the
                team did breach the regulations, there were mitigating circumstances. Specifically,
                the limited space available contributed to the situation, and the team member was only
                briefly in the fast lane. Taking these factors into account, the Stewards have decided
                to issue a reprimand to the team.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     30 - Liam Lawson
Competitor Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
Time            14:30
Session         Free Practice 1
Fact            Car 30 left the pit lane when the light at the end of the pit lane was red.
Infringement Breach of Article B1.6.3e of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        No penalty is applied.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 30, team representatives and reviewed
                positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, team radio and in-car video
                evidence.
                The driver was warned he had 7 seconds left when he left the garage. He then
                travelled down the pit lane, and the green light changed to red when he was
                approximately 0.8 seconds from crossing the pit lane exit. He then reported over the
                team radio that he had been focusing on the countdown clock which is located above
                the pit exit, which still showed two seconds remaining before the light turned red.
                The Stewards note that this countdown clock is not official and does not override the
                red light at the pit exit. There is no official synchronization between the countdown
                clock and red light at pit exit. The Stewards also note that considering the driver had
                less than a second to react, had he tried to stop he might have ended up coming to a
                halt on a live track.
                In view of the above mitigating circumstances, no penalty will be imposed.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

                Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely
                on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

Fact           The CDS did not function when the car stopped on the track.
Infringement Breach of Article C9.3 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision       The competitor (McLaren Mastercard F1 Team) is fined €30,000, €10,000 of which
               is suspended for a period of 12 months subject to no further breaches of this
               regulation.
Reason         The Stewards heard from the team Sporting Director and Technical Director Applied
               Engineering, the FIA Single Seater Sporting Director, FIA Technical Delegate, FIA
               Electronic Engineer and FIA electric and Hybrid Powertrain Engineer.
               The team admitted that for aerodynamic purposes it had placed transparent tape over
               the button that is required to be pressed to activate the CDS. This, in the opinion of
               the FIA representatives and admitted by the team, completely defeated the purpose
               of the CDS system, which is designed to be activated quickly by a marshal wearing
               protective gloves. The team conceded that it was not possible to break the tape and
               press the button by hand without the use of a tool.
               The Stewards have determined to suspend a lower amount of this penalty compared
               to a breach of this same regulation at the previous event, because that breach, and
               the subsequent penalty, should have alerted all teams to the importance of the CDS
               system.

                the end of the pit lane.
                The penalty specified by the regulation, a ten-second stop-and-go penalty was
                communicated by the stewards to Race Control. The message that was posted to
                the teams on Timing Page 3 said “Stop–And-Go”. Car 22 (VAR) entered the pit lane
                in due course came to a stop in its pit box and immediately departed without stopping
                for ten seconds. The stewards note that while a mere stop-and-go penalty is not
                among the listed penalties provided under Article 39.3, it is a penalty allowed by
                Article 12.4.1.l of the International Sporting Code. The team, having served the
                posted penalty, bears no fault in failing to serve the intended penalty. The stewards
                surmise that the confusion stems from the fact that the in the Formula 1 regulations, a
                stop-and-go penalty by definition includes an obligation to stop for ten seconds. Such
                is not the case within the F2 Sporting Regulations. Given the gap between the series
                regulations, it is imperative that penalty announcements in Formula 2 and 3 be made
                be made with clarity in these circumstances.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

               determined that Car 51 was warned multiple times that Car 16 (LEC) was arriving on
               a fast lap. Yet, Car 51 was weaving and moving well into the racing line. Car 16 had to
               take evasive action to avoid a collision by moving to the right, with a significant
               amount of the car off the track. The situation that was created was clearly dangerous
               and Car 51 should have taken more care to avoid impeding Car 16.
               While the typical penalty for impeding in a Free Practice session is a warning, in this
               instance, we are of the view that a reprimand is warranted.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    21 - James Wharton
Competitor PREMA Racing
Time           08:39
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 21 (Wharton) left the track at Turn 6 and gained a lasting advantage over Car 27
               (David)
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations
             Alleged Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (c) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code
Decision       No further action
Reason         The Stewards examined the video evidence, summoned (Documents 53 & 54), and
               heard from the Drivers of Car 21 (Wharton) and Car 27 (David).
               On the approach to Turn 6, Car 27 was on the left (inside) and Car 21 on the right,
               with Car 21 attempting to pass around the outside of the corner.
               Car 27 stated that he was ahead of Car 21 at the apex of Turn 6 and was defending
               an outside overtake attempt. He stated that, in accordance with the F2/F3 Driving
               Standards Guidelines, Car 21 did not earn entitlement to the corner.
               Car 21 stated that he had the sufficient overlap (his front axle was ahead of Car 27’s
               front axle) to be entitled to racing room, and that the lack of room left by Car 27
               forced him wide. He stated that he remained in full control of the car throughout the
               corner and was not aware that he had exceeded track limits due to the close
               proximity of the two cars. He added that, had he been aware he had left the track, he
               would have given the position back.
               Having considered the mater extensively, the Stewards were unable to definitely
               conclude, with sufficient clarity, the relative position of both cars at the apex of the
               corner. Accordingly, the Stewards decide to take no further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    27 - Yevan David
Competitor AIX Racing
Time           10:11
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 27 (David) was alleged to have forced Car 6 (De Palo) off track at Turn 15.
Infringement Alleged Breach of Appendix L Chapter IV Article 2 (b) of the FIA International Sporting
             Code
Decision       No Further Action
Reason         The Stewards reviewed the video evidence, summoned (Documents 45 & 46), and
               heard from the Drivers of Car 27 (David) and Car 6 (De Palo), together with their
               Team Representatives.
               On the approach to Turn 15, Car 27 was on the right (inside) and Car 6 on the left
               (outside), running side by side through the corner.
               The Driver of Car 27 stated that he was defending his position on the final lap of the
               race. Whilst aware that Car 6 was attempting to overtake, he maintained that Car 6
               had not satisfied the criteria under the F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines for an
               outside overtake, and had therefore not earned the right to room at the exit of Turn
               15.
               The Driver of Car 6 stated that, having gained a strong run under DRS, he drew
               alongside Car 27 and attempted to pass around the outside of Turn 15. He
               contended that Car 27 was carrying too much speed into the corner and had no
               proper means of defending his position at the exit.
               The F2/F3 Driving Standards Guidelines provide that, to be entitled to room (including
               at the exit) when overtaking on the outside of a corner, the overtaking car must: "have
               its front axle ahead of the front axle of the other car at the apex". The Stewards
               further note that overtaking on the outside of a high-speed corner carries an
               inherently greater level of risk, and the overtaking car must be ahead at the apex to
               establish entitlement to racing room.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was
               alongside, but not ahead of, Car 27 through the whole corner, and accordingly did not
               satisfy the criteria required to earn priority at the exit. As the obligation under the
               Guidelines to earn priority rests with the overtaking car, and Car 6 had not met that
               standard, the right to the corner remained with Car 27 as the defending car, and Car
               6 was not forced off by Car 27.
               Accordingly, the Stewards decide to take no further action.
              Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
             Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
             Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    6 - Nikola Tsolov
Competitor Campos Racing
Time           10:16
Session        Practice
Fact           Car 6 (Tsolov) was alleged to have breached yellow flag regulations.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Document 14) heard from the Driver of Car 6 (TSO), the
               team representatives and the FIA Technical Delegate. Together they reviewed
               positioning/marshalling system data, video evidence, timing data and telemetry.
               During the hearing the driver stated that he was aware of the yellow flag and he lifted
               the throttle until he saw the green digi panel in front of him (at the exit of Turn 13). The
               Team provided telemetry evidence taken from the car which was verified with
               the Technical Delegate as being from the section of the track that was under single
               yellow at the time.
               The Stewards determined that the driver entered Turn 12, being the commencement
               of the yellow flag sector, at a higher speed to his previous and subsequent push laps
               as he was on an improving lap time. The telemetry confirmed that the driver made a
               discernible lift increasing from 5% to 20% while within the yellow flag sector, which
               was also reflected in his speed reduction between the entry to the apex of Turn 13 in
               comparison to the other push laps. This reduction in speed was higher than on any
               other push lap. Although the margin of compliance was minimal, the Stewards were
               satisfied that given the sequence of corners and the amount of the reduction in
               speed, the driver had reduced speed in response to the yellow flag.
               Having considered all of the available evidence, the Stewards determined that the
               driver complied with the requirements of the regulations and that no breach had
               occurred. Accordingly, no further action is taken.
               The Stewards emphasise that this decision is based on the specific facts of this case
               and should not be considered as setting a precedent for future cases.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    6 - Matteo De Palo
Competitor Trident
Time           11:45
Session        Race 2
Fact           The rear diffuser of Car 6 was found to be lower than the minimum height stipulated in
               Article 3.4.1a of the 2026 FIA F3 Technical Regulations.
Infringement Article 3.4.1.a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations.
Decision       Disqualification of Car 6 from the Classification of Race 2 (Feature).
               All cars originally classified behind Car 6 are moved up one place in the Race
               classification.
               All lap times set by Car 6 during the Race are cancelled.
Reason         The Stewards, having received the report of the Technical Delegate (Document 57),
               summoned (Document 62) and heard the driver of Car 6 (De Palo), the Team
               Representative and the Race Engineer.
               The Technical Delegate reported that, following Race 2, the diffuser of Car 6 was
               found to be below the minimum height required by Article 3.4.1.a of the FIA Formula 3
               Technical Regulations. After the 5 mm tolerance under Article 3.4.2 had been taken
               into account, the diffuser measured up to 3 mm below the minimum on the right-hand
               side and 1 mm below the minimum on the left-hand side.
               The Team Representative confirmed the measurements taken by the Technical
               Delegate. The team submitted, however, that Car 6 had received a number of rear
               impacts from Car 5 (Slater), the Driver's team-mate, during Race 2, most likely in the
               diffuser area, and invited the Stewards to review the footage in support of that
               account.
               The Stewards reviewed the footage of the final two laps of Race 2 and confirmed that
               Car 5 made contact with Car 6 on two occasions during that period. The Stewards
               and the Technical Delegate inspected Car 5 and observed some damage to its front
               wing. On inspection of Car 6, the Stewards observed only very minimal scratches to
               the rear diffuser. The Race Engineer stated his belief that the contact from Car 5
               may have caused a deformation or bending of the diffuser plates.
               Article 11.7.3 of the ISC provides that, where the regulations place the burden of
               proof on the person alleged to have committed a breach, that person must satisfy the
               Stewards, on the balance of probability, that the fact asserted is more likely than not
               to be true.
              Under Article 1.4 of the Technical Regulations, the car must comply with the FIA
             Formula 3 Technical Regulations in their entirety at all times during a Competition,
             and under Article 1.8 it is the duty of the Competitor to satisfy the Technical Delegate
             and the Stewards that its car so complies. The burden of establishing compliance
             therefore rests, at all times, with the Competitor.
             The longstanding jurisprudence of the FIA International Court of Appeal (the "ICA")
             holds that a breach of the technical regulations must lead to disqualification unless
             the Competitor has committed no fault, whether intentionally or through negligence,
             and the non-conformity is the result of exceptional circumstances. These two
             conditions are cumulative, and exceptional circumstances are admitted only under
             very limited criteria. The ICA has likewise declined to accept an in-race incident as
             the cause of a technical irregularity where the physical condition of the car does not
             support that account (ICA-2014-03).
             Applying that framework, the breach is established and is not disputed. The Team
             Representative confirmed the measurements, and the Stewards are comfortably
             satisfied that the diffuser of Car 6 was below the minimum height permitted by Article
             3.4.1.a after the applicable tolerance.
             The burden then rests on the Competitor to show, on the balance of probability, that
             the car was compliant before the contact and that the contact from Car 5 caused the
             non-conformity.
             The Stewards considered whether the contact from Car 5 was, by itself, enough to
             relieve the Competitor of the consequence of the non-conformity. The Stewards
             accepted that contact occurred twice. The burden, however, was on the Competitor
             to show that it was more likely than not that the contact caused the non-conformity,
             and the Competitor produced nothing to meet it. Beyond the assertion that the contact
             may have deformed the diffuser, no evidence was put before the Stewards
             connecting the contact to the measurements found. The very minimal scratches
             observed on Car 6 showed no breakage consistent with a displacing impact. The
             Technical Delegate confirms that the diffuser assembly was properly fixed and they
             did not note any displacement or misalignment. With no evidence before them
             capable of tipping the balance of probability in the Competitor's favour, the Stewards
             cannot treat the contacts as the cause of the breach.
             The Competitor has therefore not met the burden upon it. In-race contact of this
             nature does not meet the strict and narrow criteria for exceptional circumstances
             recognized by the International Court of Appeal.
             For these reasons, and having considered the matters raised extensively, the
             Stewards find that Car 6 is in breach of Article 3.4.1.a of the 2026 FIA Formula 3
             Championship Technical Regulations, and that the Competitor has not provided
             evidence capable of relieving it of its obligation to ensure the conformity of the car.
             The Stewards therefore issue the disqualification as a standard penalty for a
             technical infringement.
             Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
             Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
             Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact          A non operational member of team personnel was reported as seated on a pit wall
              stand.
Infringement Breach of Article 22.12 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision      A fine of 1000 Euros to be paid by the Competitor. Payment of 500 Euros be made
              immediately, The remaining 500 Euros are suspended, subject to no similar breach
              during the 2026 F2 Season In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the ISC, fines shall
              be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank transfer to the
              FIA.
Reason        The Stewards summoned (Document 19) and heard the team representative. They
              examined photographic evidence and reviewed the Team Operational Declaration.
              The Team Manager explained that the gentleman involved is a team guest, although
              this person is registered as non-operational personnel, the Team Manager was
              unaware that the gentleman had been invited by a member of the F1 Experiences
              team to occupy a pit wall position that was not operational at the time. He was also
              provided with a headset from F1 Experiences carrying the live circuit commentary.
              Having considered all of the available evidence, the Stewards determined that,
              irrespective of whether the pit wall position was operational, this person, being
              registered as non-operational personnel, was not permitted to be on the pit wall during
              a live session. This constitutes a breach of Article 21.12 of the 2026 FIA Formula 2
              Sporting Regulations.
              The Stewards accepted that there was no intention on the part of the Team to gain
              any sporting advantage and took into account the particular circumstances of the
              case, and hence partially suspended the fine.
              Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
              Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
              Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (documents 42 & 43)
and heard from the drivers and team representatives, have considered the following matter and
determine the following:

No / Driver     11 - Sergio Perez
Competitor Cadillac Formula 1 Team
Time            17:38
Session         Sprint
Fact            Car 11 collided with Car 18 in Turn 16
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision        No penalty is applied.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 18 (Lance Stroll), the driver of Car 11
                (Sergio Perez), team representatives and reviewed video and in-car video evidence.
                Car 11 attempted to overtake Car 18 on the inside into Turn 16 and both cars made
                contact. The Stewards determine that the driver of Car 11 initiated the overtaking
                attempt in a legitimate way, but then locked up the front right wheel therefore was not
                able to rotate the car anymore.
                The Stewards determine the the driver of Car 11 was predominantly at fault, but also
                take into account the weather conditions and acknowledge the difficulties of
                controlling the car on the brakes in such circumstances. Therefore a 5 second time
                penalty is deemed appropriate and would have been applied in-race if that had been
                possible. As Car 11 was not classified and 5 second time penalties regularly do not
                convert into grid drops, no penalty is applied in this case.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

                Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely
                on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

               The driver of Car 1 attempted to overtake Car 81 on the inside at Turn 5. A collision
               occurred at the apex.

               and, after turning in, noticed Car 1 on the inside and attempted to leave space. The
               driver of Car 1 said that he saw an opportunity to overtake. He said that the front axle

               to be left space. As he approached the apex, the space was less than he had

               The Stewards considered that both drivers had contributed to the incident and that

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (document 44) and
heard from the driver and team representative, have considered the following matter and determine
the following:

No / Driver     41 - Arvid Lindblad
Competitor Visa Cash App Racing Bulls F1 Team
Time            17:44
Session         Sprint
Fact            The Driver drove in the wrong direction at Turn 5
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 12.2.1.h of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 41 (Arvid Lindblad), team representative
                and reviewed video and in-car video evidence.
                Car 41 spun after the exit of Turn 5 and was facing towards oncoming cars. Car 41
                drove in the wrong direction for approximately 100 metres back to Turn 5 and used
                the run-off area to turn around.
                The Driver explained that he could not perform a flick turn from the position in which
                his car was stopped after the spin. Because he was facing the wrong way, he drove
                back a short distance against oncoming traffic but staying to the edge of the track
                and away from the racing line. After he was sure the last car had passed, the Driver
                of Car 41 attempted a flick turn but the car would not rotate. The Driver explained
                that, knowing that the last car had passed and it would present no danger for him to
                continue, he drove back to turn 5 where he knew there would be space to turn.
                Having regard to the difficult position the Driver of Car 41 found himself in, where his
                car was originally prone and then unable to turn, and given further that there was no
                oncoming traffic, the Stewards determined that what occurred was not in these
                circumstances unsafe and therefore took no further action.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.
