The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, summoned (documents 63 & 64)
and heard from the drivers and team representatives, have considered the following matter and
determine the following:

No / Driver     27 - Nico Hulkenberg
Competitor Audi Revolut F1 Team
Time            22:10
Session         Qualifying
Fact            Car 27 impeded Car 55 in turn 5
Infringement Breach of Article B4.1.1 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        No penalty applied
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 27 (Nico Hulkenberg), the driver of Car
                55 (Carlos Sainz), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system
                data, video, team radio, timing and in-car video evidence.
                Video showed that Car 27 was driving slowly on the racing line on the approach to
                turn 5. Car 55 arrived from behind on a push lap and had to abandon the lap. That
                Car 55 was thereby impeded was not in dispute. The issue was whether Car 55 had
                been ‘unnecessarily’ impeded.
                The team stated in the hearing that they believed, based on timing information to
                which they subscribed, sourced from the official timekeeping provider, that Car 55
                had already taken the chequered flag and conveyed that information to the driver by
                radio. Therefore the driver of Car 27 did not expect Car 55 to still be on a push lap
                when it was closing in.
                The Stewards acknowledge the fact that the data referenced by the team led the team
                to reasonably believe that Car 55 had received the chequered flag. Indeed, it was
                evident from Car 55’s radio messages that its team had formed the same belief
                relying on the same data.
                The misunderstanding was revealed to be attributable to the information initially
                received by the teams not being fully synchronised and only being displayed in a
                correct manner after a short period of time. However, that post-processing did not
                occur until Car 55 arrived behind Car 27 depriving the team of any reasonable
                opportunity to correct the information conveyed to the driver.
                In the Stewards’ assessment, because the source of the data upon which the team
                relied was the official timing provider, it was not unreasonable for the team to have
                relied upon it, even though the team also had available to it the official timing data
                which conflicted.
                On the objective facts, the Stewards determined that Car 55 was unnecessarily
               impeded. However, there were extraordinary mitigating circumstances in this case
               because the incident was attributable to the team’s reliance on information that was,
               for a brief period, inconsistent.

No / Driver     3 - Max Verstappen
Competitor Oracle Red Bull Racing
Time            20:35
Session         Sprint Qualifying
Fact            Car 3 overtook Car 44 under single yellow flags.
Infringement Breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5b of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision        No penalty is applied.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 3 (Max Verstappen), the driver of Car 44
                (Lewis Hamilton), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system
                data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence.
                As Car 3 was exiting turn 7 on a push lap, a single yellow flag was displayed. Car 44
                was ahead of Car 3 and had been warned of Car 3’s approach. The Driver of Car 44
                said that after exiting turn 7, he slowed and moved to the right to ensure he was off
                the racing line. Car 3 overtook Car 44 prior to turn 8 while both cars were still in the
                yellow flag sector. Car 3 then abandoned the push lap.
                The Driver of Car 3 explained that he was on throttle exiting turn 7 and then saw the
                yellow flag and lifted. This was confirmed by telemetry. Within approximately 40
                metres of entering the yellow flag sector, the Driver of Car 3 had lifted fully off throttle.
                The Driver of Car 44 was braking and had reduced speed to less than 60km/h at the
                point Car 3 overtook. Because Car 3 was on a push lap and was on throttle out of
                turn 7 and Car 44 had slowed, the speed differential at the point of the overlap was
                significant despite the fact that the Driver of Car 3 had also started braking.
                The Stewards were satisfied that the Driver of Car 3 reacted appropriately to the
                yellow flag by lifting off throttle and reducing speed. The speed of Car 3 at the
                overtake point was some 70km/h less than Car 3’s speed on another push lap in the
                same session.
                The Driver of Car 3 explained that to have avoided the overtake would have required
                him to have braked very heavily and he considered to have done so would have
                potentially created an unsafe situation.
                The Stewards determined that the Driver of Car 3 breached the yellow flag regulation
                by overtaking Car 44. However, the Stewards were satisfied that the overtake was an
                unfortunate consequence of the significant closing speed differential and, in these
                circumstances, determined not to impose a penalty.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    10 - Taito Kato
Competitor ART Grand Prix
Time           10:05
Session        Race 1
Fact           Cars 1 (Nael) and 10 (Kato) were in close quarters at Turn 18 and Car 10 went off
               track and reentered in front of Car 1.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 27.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and
               team representatives (documents 67 & 68).
               The Stewards were requested to investigate the overall interaction of Car 1 (NAE)
               and Car 10 (KAT) at Turn 18. The investigation commenced from a neutral point of
               view meaning that neither party was alleged to be the primary offender. Instead, the
               Stewards examined related but separate questions: whether NAE forced KAT off
               track in between Turns 18 and 19 or whether KAT left the track at the exit of Turn 18
               and gained a lasting advantage by doing so.
               Article 27.3 of the Formula 3 Sporting Regulations provides that once a car has gone
               off track it may re-join provided it does so “without gaining any lasting advantage”.
               Gaining a position constitutes gaining an advantage as does failing to lose a position
               that should have fairly been lost.
               In order to judge whether a position was gained or lost we must first determine the
               relative positions before and after. In this case the cars were in such close quarters
               at the apex of Turn 18 that it cannot be determined who was ahead at the point the
               cars should be judged. The Stewards, therefore, cannot make a clear determination
               whether KAT gained a position or merely retained one. If KAT was forced off while
               ahead, he is entitled to retain the position. To the contrary, if NAE had won the
               corner, he is not liable for forcing KAT off, and KAT would be obligated to lose the
               position. Since Document 69 was inconclusive as to whether or not NAE forced KAT
               off, it is impossible to determine here whether or not the circumstances required KAT
               to be behind NAE after re-joining to avoid retaining an unfair advantage. Based on
               the totality of these very narrow circumstances, the Stewards are not comfortably
               satisfied that KAT committed an infraction, and we therefore elect to take no further
               action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
              Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    17 - Tasanapol Inthraphuvasak
Competitor ART Grand Prix
Time           10:18
Session        Race 2
Fact           Alleged unsafe release from Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) when Car 15 (Dunne) was in
               the fast lane.
Infringement Breach of Article 28.12 (a) of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 67 & 68) and heard the Drivers of Car 17
               (Inthraphuvasak) and Car 15 (Dunne) and the team representatives. They
               examined video evidence.
               Car 15 entered the pit lane ahead of Car 17 both carrying out their mandatory pit
               stops. Car 15 was held in his pit position in order for another car to pass in the fast
               lane. This delay combined with perhaps a faster stop by car 17 resulted in Car 17
               being released just after car 15 but in the pit position further ahead in the lane and
               hence ahead in position.
               When the driver of Car 17 was signalled to go, Car 15 was just leaving his pit area
               but was not yet in the fast lane. The Stewards used the other car in the fast lane as a
               reference point for the release of both Car 15 and 17 and concluded that each was
               released in a similar fashion relative to that car. Car 17 experienced some wheel
               spin when leaving his pit position and joined the fast lane immediately ahead of Car
               15 but they were momentarily along side each other. The available space for Car 15
               reduced as the two cars converged, and the driver of Car 15 elected to lift and fall
               behind Car 17. Car 17 was also seen to take avoiding action and briefly straddled
               the painted area in the pit lane separating the fast lane from the working lane.
               In judging if an unsafe release had occurred the Stewards assessed the
               circumstances at the point Car 17 completely cleared its pit-stop position, as required
               by Article 28.12 and also considered the point that the release signal was given to
               Car 17 and concluded that there was sufficient gap for the release to be done safely.
                The subsequent convergence between Cars 15 and 17 arose from simultaneous
               movement and Car 17’s wheelspin rather than an objectively unsafe gap at the
               release point. At all times both drivers were fully aware of each other and managed
               the situation appropriately.
               At the hearing the stewards were asked to consider whether either car had breached
            a regulation by driving along side each other briefly. Given the entire circumstances
           and how the drivers managed the situation the Stewards did not find that this reached
           to the level of a breach of the regulations either.

           Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
           Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact           Cars 1 (Nael) and 10 (Kato) were in close quarters at Turn 18 and Car 10 went off
               track and reentered in front of Car 1.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, 2b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the drivers and
               team representatives (documents 67 & 68).
               The stewards were requested to investigate the overall interaction of Car 1 (NAE)
               and Car 10 (KAT) at Turn 18. The investigation commenced from a neutral point of
               view meaning that neither party was alleged to be the primary offender. Instead, the
               Stewards examined separate but related questions: whether NAE forced KAT off
               track in between Turns 18 and 19 or whether KAT left the track at the exit of Turn 18
               and gained a lasting advantage by doing so.
               Clearly NAE had his front axle at KAT’s mirror at the apex of T18. However, a driver
               attempting an inside overtake is expected to have his front axle to the mirror prior to
               and at the apex. Additional considerations are how the cars arrived to the apex (was
               the manoeuvre made too late or was it overly optimistic?). In this borderline case, the
               Stewards are not comfortably satisfied that NAE established his position early
               enough to have won the corner. Neither are we comfortably satisfied that he failed to
               do so. If he had won the corner he would not be guilty of forcing KAT off. Being
               unable to determine whether or not NAE had won the rights to the corner it cannot be
               fairly determined whether or not he is liable for forcing KAT off. Since the Stewards
               have not reached the threshold of being comfortably satisfied with their conclusion,
               we refrain from taking any further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact            Car 24 (Van Hoepen) was allegedly the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Document 24) and heard the Driver of Car 24 (Van
                Hoepen) and the team representative.
                Car 24 stopped on the circuit after suffering a gearbox failure, which resulted in the
                session being red flagged. The FIA Technical Delegate confirmed through the
                recorded data that the gearbox malfunction prevented the driver from selecting gears
                and that the failure was caused by a genuine technical failure.
                Having considered the matter extensively and having consulted with the FIA Technical
                Delegate, the Stewards determined that, whilst Car 24 was the immediate cause of
                the red flag, the driver could not be regarded as the sole cause of the red flag within
                the meaning of Article 33.5 of the Sporting Regulations.
                Article 33.5 provides the Stewards with the discretion to determine whether the
                deletion of the driver's fastest qualifying lap is warranted where a driver is the sole
                cause of a red flag. The purpose of the Article is to address situations in which a
                driver's actions have unfairly compromised the qualifying attempts of other
                competitors.
                In the present case, the evidence establishes that the red flag resulted from an
                unforeseen mechanical failure outside the driver's control. The driver neither
                contributed to nor could reasonably have avoided the incident. Accordingly, the
                Stewards find that the circumstances do not justify the deletion of the driver's fastest
                qualifying lap.

                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact           Car 8 (Bilinski) was alleged to have failed to respect double waved yellow flags at
               Turn 19.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix H, Article 2.5.5 (b) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Document 29) and heard the Driver of Car 8 (Bilinski) and
               the team representatives. Together they examined the available video evidence,
               marshalling system data and timing and telemetry data.
               The sector under evaluation was the last sector of the track starting at the exit of
               Turn 19 and ending at the Control line. In comparing the sector times it is relevant to
               understand that the ideal line for the start of a push lap yields a faster sector time
               than is achieved when the sector is the last one of a push lap. This is because the
               drivers are able to make a different exit from Turn 19 when not following the T18 to
               T19 sequence. As a result an initial view of the sector times gave the impression that
               the driver may not have respected the double yellow requirements.
               Looking at the detailed telemetry data showed that the driver had lifted significantly
               and went back to throttle later in reaction to the double yellow. So although the sector
               time may not have shown an increase in time the drivers reaction did reflect the
               appropriate action. Accordingly the Stewards concluded that the driver did respect
               the requirements in this particular case.

               having already decided to perform his practice start, launched and had to pass to
               avoid.

               perform a practice start if another car in front of him is still stationary ahead on the
               same side of the grid.” Since the car in front was moving, it cannot be said that CLE
               violated that instruction, however the ISC provision against unsafe acts remains to be
               considered. In this case, the Stewards determine that CLE acted unsafely by
               performing his practice start before allowing the car in front to safely clear its grid
               position. Fortunately, this manoeuvre was not unsafe with respect to other cars.
               While CLE’s practice start did not expressly violate the Competition Notes, the
               Stewards determine that a warning is in order for failing to wait a reasonable amount
               of time before commencing his practice start.

               any lasting advantage”. Because ESC was defending, he would be expected to

               was not entitled. Failing to lose a position that should have fairly been lost constitutes
               gaining an advantage.

               with a car in front. The Stewards accept that the field was displaying multiple
               instances of erratic driving during the lap in question but determine that STR had
               every reason to expect it to continue. Under the circumstances, the Stewards
               conclude that it was not reasonable for STR to assume that cars would begin driving
               normally out of Turn 13 and that he had every reason to take extra caution in this
               situation. While the driving throughout the entire pack factored into the collision, the
               Stewards find STR to be predominantly at fault for running into the rear of DAV. The
               penalty imposed is in accordance with the penalty guidelines.

Infringement Breach of Article 21.5 and Appendix 5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       - 20.000€ fine to be paid by the Competitor. In accordance with Article 12.8.1 of the
               ISC, fines shall be paid within forty‐eight hours of their notification by means of bank
               transfer to the FIA
               - Disqualification of Car 5 from the Feature Race (Race 2). All cars originally

               during the remainder of the 2026 F2 Season..
Reason         The Stewards examined the available evidence, summoned the Drivers and Team
               Manager (documents 69, 73 & 74). As the driver Noel LEON had already left the
               track, they only heard from Nikola TSOLOV and the Team Manager.
               A person declared as Non-Operational Personnel was observed wearing a radio
               headset fitted with a microphone, and therefore had the appearance of potentially
               being able to transit, and therefore not a “listen only headset”. This is alleged to be a
               breach of Appendix 5 and Article 21.5 of the F2 Sporting Regulations. Under the
               applicable regulations, Non-Operational Personnel may only be in possession of a
               listen-only radio headset.
               During the hearing, the Team Manager explained that the person concerned, who
               was a team guest, had inadvertently taken the wrong type of headset.
               The Stewards noted that the team guest had been approached by a Scrutineer and
               informed that the headset was not permitted as it was fitted with a microphone. The
               Scrutineer was advised in response that the microphone was folded upwards.
               Despite having been specifically advised that the headset was not permitted, the team
               guest subsequently put the headset back on and continued to use it.
            Nevertheless, the Team remains responsible for ensuring that radio equipment
           provided to Non-Operational Personnel and team guests complies with the applicable
           requirements. The regulations in this respect are clear: Non-Operational Personnel
           may only be in possession of a listen-only radio headset. The Team is expected to
           exercise greater care in controlling the allocation and use of such equipment.
           In determining the scope of the penalty, the Stewards also established that the team
           guest concerned was associated exclusively with Car 5 and had no involvement with
           the Team’s other car. The Stewards therefore considered that it would not be
           appropriate to apply the sporting consequence of this infringement to the other car
           and determined that the disqualification should apply only to Car 5.
           Furthermore, the team guest was observed using the non-compliant headset only
           during this session. There was no evidence before the Stewards that the guest had
           used the headset during any other session of the Competition. The Stewards
           therefore determined that the disqualification should be limited to Car 5 from the
           results of this session only.
           The Stewards emphasise that it remains the responsibility of the Team to ensure
           compliance with these requirements and to put appropriate measures in place to
           prevent any recurrence.
           Taking into account the circumstances above, the Stewards apply the above
           mentioned penalties.

Fact           Car 5 (Leon) was the sole cause of the issuance of the red flag.
Infringement Breach of Article 33.5 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       Car 5 is determined to have been the sole cause of the Red Flag issued at 16:00
               hours
               Deletion of all lap times set during the Qualifying Session after the Red Flag which
               was issued at 16:00 hours
               No lap time was set prior to the Red Flag, so the Stewards were unable to delete the
               fastest lap set prior to the Red Flag
               Start permission given for both Races, to be placed on the grid in accordance with
               Article 34.2 of the F2 Sporting Regulations
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Document 23) and heard the Driver of Car 5 (Leon) and
               the team representative. They reviewed video evidence and determined that, at the
               start of the Qualifying Session, Car 5 was on its out-lap. While negotiating the apex of
               Turn 4, Car 5 lost control, spun and came to a stop on the left-hand side of the track
               at the exit of Turn 4. A red flag was subsequently declared by the Race Director. Car
               5 was then able to restart the car without assistance and followed the red flag
               procedure, proceeding directly to the Pit Lane.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards noted that the track had been
               declared wet by the Race Director prior to the commencement of the session. The
               Driver of Car 5 was therefore aware of the prevailing track conditions when entering
               Turn 4. Having reviewed the available evidence, the Stewards determined that no
               external factors contributed to the spin and that the incident was solely caused by the
               Driver of Car 5. Consequently, the Driver of Car 5 was determined to be solely
               responsible for the incident which resulted in the red flag.
               During the hearing, the Team Representative indicated that he had sought permission
               from the Race Director for the Driver to continue. As the incident had not yet been
               investigated by the Stewards and no decision on the Sole Cause of the Red Flag had
               been determined, the Race Director properly responded that the Driver could
               continue. It has been agreed with the teams that the Sole Cause of a Red Flag will be
               investigated after a session when it is not absolutely clear to the Stewards that there
               was no mechanical or other cause outside the control of the Driver. Considering the
            unique sequence of events in this case, the Stewards determined that they would not
           immediately hold the driver responsible and hence permitted him to continue. It was
           the driver's choice to continue in the session, knowing that all times set thereafter
           may have been invalidated.
           The Stewards, therefore, decided to invalidate all lap times set by Car 5 after the red
           flag was issued. No lap time was set prior to the Red Flag, so the Stewards were
           unable to delete the fastest lap set prior to the Red Flag. Car 5 therefore has no valid
           lap time recorded during the qualifying session.
           Finally, considering that car 5 set a suitable lap time within the 107% limit during free
           practice session, the Stewards permit Car 5 to start both Races behind all the
           classified drivers.

Time           10:18
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 6 (De Palo) left the track at Turn 5, ran through the runoff, rejoined the track after
               Turn 6 and retained position over Car 28 (Barrichello).
Infringement Breach of Article 27.3 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F3
               Sporting Regulations. No driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence.
               The video shows Car 6 (DEP) was approaching Turn 5 with Car 28 (BAR) side-by-
               side in the braking zone. DEP missed the corner while defending, ran off the track
               and rejoined after Turn 6 ahead of BAR. Article 27.3 of the Formula 3 Sporting
               Regulations provides that once a car has gone off track it may re-join provided it
               does so “without gaining any lasting advantage”. Because DEP was defending, he
               would be expected to concede the position. Because he did not do so he retained a
               position to which he was not entitled. Failing to lose a position that should have fairly
               been lost constitutes gaining an advantage.
               The Stewards consider this to be an infringement and impose the baseline penalty
               which is consistent with penalties for breaches of a similar nature.

               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

               (Beganovic) and Car 2 (Durksen) and the team representatives. They
               examined video evidence.
               During the Formation Lap, Cars 14, 8, 2 and 7 were travelling in sequence. Upon
               exiting Turn 17, Car 14 reduced its speed, which caused Cars 8 and 2 to slow
               accordingly. Car 7 was approaching at a higher speed and, upon realising that the
               cars ahead had slowed significantly, took evasive action by moving to the right-hand
               side of the track. In doing so, Car 7 left the track and overtook Cars 14, 8 and 2.
               Before entering Turn 18, Car 7 allowed all three cars to re-pass, thereby re-
               establishing its original starting order.
               During the hearing, the driver of Car 7 stated that he had been surprised by the
               speed of Car 14, which, in his view, was unusually slow at that point of the track. He
               explained that, upon realising the significant reduction in speed of the cars ahead, he
               took all reasonable measures to avoid a potential collision.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that the driver of
               Car 7 should have been more aware of the speed at which the cars ahead were
               travelling. As a consequence of failing to do so, the driver was required to take
               evasive action to avoid a potential collision with Cars 8 and 2, leaving the track and
               overtaking multiple cars during the Formation Lap. The Stewards nevertheless
               accepted the driver’s explanation that the speed of Car 14 at the exit of Turn 17 was
               unusually slow for that section of the circuit.
               The Stewards concluded that, notwithstanding the circumstances described above,
               the driver of Car 7 remained responsible for controlling his speed and ensuring that
               he did not overtake other cars during the Formation Lap. Consequently, they decided
               to impose a warning to the driver of car 7.

               with Car 8.

               situation, with multiple cars negotiating a tight hairpin simultaneously and the available
               space reducing rapidly. Nevertheless, the Stewards determined that Car 8 had no
               realistic opportunity to avoid the collision, as it was constrained by another car to its
               left and was entitled to follow its chosen racing line through the corner.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards concluded that the driver of
               Car 9 was wholly responsible for the collision. While acknowledging the challenging
               circumstances of the opening lap at Turn 1, the Stewards determined that the driver
               of Car 9 failed to maintain sufficient control of the car under braking and was solely
               responsible for the resulting contact with Car 8. The Stewards therefore imposed a 5-
               second time penalty on the driver of Car 9.

 Decision         No further action.

 Reasons          The Stewards thoroughly reviewed Marshalling/Positioning data, timing data, on-board cameras and
                  CCTV cameras.

                  majority of the circuit. However, in all cases the Stewards determined that the drivers took appropriate
                 actions to not impede other drivers, and in all cases, they slowed down significantly to allow other
                drivers to pass while giving those drivers a clear track. The Stewards therefore determine that all drivers
                concerned did not drive “unnecessarily slowly”, and that they were above the maximum time because
                they took appropriate steps, and we therefore take no further action.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    15 - Alex Dunne
Competitor Rodin Motorsport
Time           10:59
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 15 (Dunne) was alleged to have forced Car 1 (Camara) off track at Turn 3.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L Chapter IV, Article 2 (b) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 41 & 42) and heard the Drivers of Car 15
               (Dunne) and Car 1 (Camara) and the team representatives. They examined
               video evidence.
               On the run to Turn 3 Car 1 made and outside pass on Car 15. Car 1 was ahead
               approaching the corner but the race continued towards the apex. At the apex the
               cars were almost alongside each other with Car 1 possibly a few centimetres ahead.
               At the hearing the driver of Car 1 reported that he made a clean pass on the outside
               and felt he was fully ahead at the apex and entitled to room on the exit. He felt that
               the driver of Car 15 should have conceded the corner and not forced him off. He had
               to take evasive action went over the sausage kerb and lost time and position to Car
               15.
               The driver of Car 15 said that he was aware that Car 1 was making and outside pass
               and he left him room. However at the apex he was squeezed by Car 1 on to the kerb
               to his left. This unsettled the car and caused him to have to adjust his line. He
               explained that he had no intention of forcing Car 1 off but he was left with no option in
               his racing line due to being forced over the kerb on the inside.
               The Stewards were unable to conclude which car was ahead at the apex even after
               looking at multiple angles for an extended period. In the circumstances and
               considering that neither driver appeared to breach the Driving Standard Guidelines
               they have elected to take no further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact           Car 23 (Shin) and Car 28 (Barrichello) had a collision at Turn 4.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. Car 23 (SHI) was attempting an outside
               pass on Car 28 (BAR) at Turn 4. SHI was trailing slightly at the apex and had not
               earned the rights to the corner. The cars maintained overlap with BAR pulling ahead
               from the apex to the exit. A collision occurred as they tracked out to the exit curb.
                Typically, such a collision would be charged to the car on the outside that had not
               established its rights, however the Stewards note that BAR on the inside tracked out
               earlier than normal for the corner which played into the collision with BAR who could
               not simply disappear. Under the circumstances the Stewards determine that neither
               driver was wholly or predominantly at fault for the collision. Accordingly, the Stewards
               elect to take no further action.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    2 - Joshua Duerksen
Competitor Invicta Racing
Time           14:18
Session        Race 1
Fact           Contact from Car 2 (Durksen) to Car 6 (Tsolov) on Lap 1 at Turn 3.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code.
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 25 & 26) and heard the Drivers of Car 2
               (Durksen) and Car 6 (Tsolov) and the team representatives. Together they examined
               video evidence and onboard footage.
               On the first lap on the exit of Turn 2, Car 2 was in 10th place passing Car 5 on the
               inside and approaching Turn 3. Ahead of them both an incident occurs between Car
               1 and Car 17 causing Car 17 to spin and crash into Car 10. In reaction to this
               incident Car 6, who is ahead of Car 2, and also on the inside with a full view of the
               incident ahead slows more than anticipated. Car 2 has no view of the incident that is
               unfolding and is caught out by how quickly Car 6 slows, and Car 2 crashes into the
               rear of Car 6 causing him to lose control.
               At the hearing Car 6 reported that he slowed more than he anticipated in reaction to
               the incident ahead in an attempt to avoid it. He reported that he was hit from behind
               and this caused him to go across the inside of Turn 3 thereby avoiding the incident on
               the track ahead.
               The Stewards concluded from the testimony of the drivers that the contact initiated by
               Car 2 was a consequence of the other incident and therefore do not find that the
               driver of Car 2 was wholly or predominantly at fault. As it is therefore a driving
               incident the Stewards elect to take no further action.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    5 - Noel Leon
Competitor Campos Racing
Time           11:09
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 5 (Leon) was alleged to have forced Car 24 (Van Hoepen) off track at Turn 4.
Infringement Alleged breach of Appendix L Chapter IV, Article 2 (b) of the FIA International
             Sporting Code
Decision       No further action.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 43 & 44) and heard the Drivers of Car 5
               (Leon) and Car 24 (Van Hoepen) and the team representatives. They examined
               video evidence.
               The Driver of Car 24 told the Stewards that he was on a different race strategy to
               Car 5 and for this reason he was faster than Car 5 at this stage of the race. He said
               that he caught up to Car 5 on the approach to Turn 4 and decided to pass on the
               outside. He said that he came alongside Car 5 and was ahead of it at the apex of
               Turn 4 and had earned priority at the exit pursuant to the Driving Standard
               Guidelines. He said that Car 5 did not provide him with room on the exit as a result of
               which he was forced off the circuit to the left and lost momentum and Car 5 remained
               in front of him.
               The Driver of Car 5 acknowledged to the Stewards that Car 24 was on a different
               race strategy, had caught him in the approach to Turn 4 and commenced an
               overtaking manoeuvre on the outside, but said that Car 24 had not earned priority in
               accordance with the Driving Standard Guidelines and that he retained priority. He
               further said that he considered Car 24 had run on to the marbles that accumulated on
               the outside of Turn 4 and suggested that was the cause for Car 24 to leave the circuit
               to the left.
               Both drivers confirmed to the Stewards that there was no contact between the cars to
               caused Car 24 to leave the circuit. The Stewards accept both drivers provided an
               honest account of their version of events.
               The only available vision of the incident was not of sufficient clarity for the Stewards
               to determine whether Car 24 had in fact earned priority pursuant to the Driving
               Standard Guidelines. The Stewards also note that a car attempting an overtaking
               manoeuvre on the outside of a corner is making a more difficult manoeuvre to
               accomplish.
            As the Stewards are not sufficiently satisfied that Car 5 forced Car 24 off the circuit
           at the exit of Turn 4 and take no further action.
           Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
           Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

The Stewards, having received a report from the Technical Delegate, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    12 - Kanato Le
Competitor ART Grand Prix
Time           13:39
Session        Race 1
Fact           Car 12 (Le) was found to be 3kg below the required minimum weight of 729kg.
Infringement Breach of Article 4.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
Decision       Disqualification of Car 12 from the Classification of Race 1.
               All cars originally classified behind Car 12 are moved up one place in the Race
               classification.
Reason         The Stewards received a report from the Technical Delegate (Document 47). They
               summoned and heard the Driver and Team Representative (Document 48).
               The Technical Delegate reported that Car 12 (KLE) was weighed after Race 1 and
               was found to be 726kg, which is 3.0kg below the minimum weight of 729kg - as
               stipulated in Article 4.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Technical Regulations.
               The Team Representative explained that they have conducted a preliminary
               investigation into the cause of being below the minimum weight and found that Car
               12’s water pressure dropped significantly after the car got hit by some gravel due to
               another car going off track. The team argued that the loss of liquid from the car’s
               cooling system was the cause of being below the minimum weight. The Stewards
               thanked the Team Representative for bringing forward this explanation and
               justification. Unfortunately the team had no way of proving the weight of the fluid lost
               or that the car was compliant before the loss.
               The Stewards reminded the Team Representative of the International Court of
               Appeal’s (ICA) long-standing and consistent jurisprudence that the obligation to
               comply with the technical regulations and the liability incurred as a result of
               noncompliance lie solely with competitors. Furthermore, the Stewards also explained
               that the long-standing sanction and ICA jurisprudence for a technical compliance has
               been a sanction of disqualification.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine this is breach of
               Article 4.1 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Championship Technical Regulations and
               accordingly decided to disqualify Car 12 from the F3 Sprint race results.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    14 - Martinius Stenshorne
Competitor Rodin Motorsport
Time           10:49
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 14 (Stenshorne) failed to complete the mandatory pit stop.
Infringement Breach of Article 38.9 b of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       Stop & Go Penalty assessed after the race – Car 14 was assessed a stop and go
               penalty which, since it could not be served during the race, was converted to a 30
               second time penalty in the final classification in accordance with Article 39.3. No
               driver penalty points are associated with this infringement.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Document 45) and heard the Driver of Car 14
               (Stenshorne) and the team representative. The Stewards examined video & GPS
               evidence.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determine that Car 14 was
               on the section of track leading to the pit lane when VSC was implemented. While he
               was committed to pitting, he had not yet reached the dotted line defining the pit entry
               as described in the Race Director Competition Notes when the VSC was displayed.
               Car 14 continued to pit and performed a tyre change. This pit stop did not satisfy the
               mandatory pit stop requirement since the mandatory pit stop cannot be performed
               under VSC unless the driver is already in the pit entry or pit lane. The Stewards
               appreciate that the driver was close to the specified pit entry line when the VSC was
               implemented and completely understand why he did what he did. However, Article
               38.9 of the Formula 2 Sporting Regulations makes it clear that a pit stop made under
               VSC does not count as the mandatory pit stop unless the Driver was already in pit
               entry road. Accordingly, the Stewards determine that Car 14 did not perform its
               mandatory pit stop. In determining the Stop and Go penalty which was converted to 30
               seconds, the Stewards considered the mandatory penalties for similar offences,
               namely entering the pit lane when it is closed and for failing to complete a mandatory
               pit stop during a race that is suspended and not resumed.

               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

               not successful.

               followed the Driving Standard Guidelines by safely making moves designed to break
               the tow. None of the moves were in reaction to an attack from the following driver.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following

No / Driver    1 - Rafael Camara
Competitor Invicta Racing
Time           14:18
Session        Race 1
Fact           Contact from Car 1 (Camara) to Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) on Lap 1 at Turn 3.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       Five seconds (5) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (a) of the FIA F2
               Sporting Regulations. In addition, 1 point is to be added to the driver’s record. Total
               for the 2026 season = 2 points
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 27 & 28) and heard the Drivers of Car 1
               (Camara) and Car 17 (Inthraphuvasak) and the team representatives and
               investigated the incident involving contact between the front of Car 1 and the rear of
               Car 17 at Turn 3 on Lap 1 of the Race. The Stewards reviewed the available video of
               the incident, which included vision from the in-car camera from Car 1 and front and
               side external views of the incident, and heard from the Drivers and the Team
               Representatives from both cars.
               The Driver of Car 17 told the Stewards that his concentration was on the cars in front
               of him when at the turn-in point for Turn 3 there was contact with the rear of his car,
               causing it to spin and collide with other vehicles. He said that he did not brake early
               and was close to the car in front of him. The Driver of Car 1 said that he was behind
               Car 17 in the approach to Turn 3 and that he was readying to brake. He felt he was in
               full control of his car. He said that there was a group of cars in front of him that all
               were racing through Turn 3 and that there was a concertina affect, which caught him
               out when braking. He said that there was only a light touch between the front of his
               car and the rear of Car 17.
               The onboard images from Car 1 shows that the driver confirms it was the following
               car and that the Driver had full vision of what was occurring in front of him and that he
               had an opportunity to have braked early and avoid the collision. For this reason, the
               Stewards find that the Driver of Car 1 was wholly to blame for causing the collision
               and therefore in breach of the rules.
               The usual penalty for causing a collision is a 10 second Time Penalty. In this
               instance the Stewards find there were mitigating factors existing to warrant a
               reduction of the usual penalty to a 5 second Time Penalty, which are that the incident
               happened on the first lap while there were a large group of cars competing for space
            which created a concertina effect.

Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence and summoned and heard the driver and
               team representative (Document 22). Car 30 entered the pit lane, approached its
               garage, and was stopped by a team mechanic in the fast lane. The team then pushed
               the car back, which blocked the fast lane and delayed five cars behind it.
               The representative accepted that the team made an error by positioning the
               mechanic in the fast lane and instructing Car 30 to stop there. The Driver of Car 30
               stated that he followed the mechanic’s instructions and believed he had stopped in the
               correct position to be pushed back.

               stopping Car 30 in the fast lane and causing the obstruction. Therefore, a
               proportionate fine is imposed on the team.

No / Driver    9 - Alessandro Giusti

Time           15:30
Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 9 (Giusti) impeded car 19 (Ho) at Turn 3
Infringement Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 b) of the FIA International Sporting Code and Article
             31.6 of the 2026 FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
Decision       A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint and Feature Races at this Competition.
               There are no penalty points associated with this decision.
Reason         The Stewards examined video and GPS telemetry evidence. They summoned and
               heard the Drivers and Team Representatives (Documents 23 & 24).
               With time winding down in the qualifying session, Car 9 (GIU) commenced a push lap,
               exceeded track limits at Turn 1, and rejoined in front of CHO with 10 seconds
               remaining on the session clock. CHO, who had a clean run through turn 1, was
               closing on GIU after his re-entry. At this point GIU’s session was effectively over
               since time was up and his lap was destined to be deleted. GIU explained that he
               continued at full pace hoping to get another push lap in. Unfortunately, GIU’s team
               had not informed him that the session was over. CHO caught GIU at T3. GIU slowed
               significantly more than CHO at Turn 3 before ultimately letting him pass on the exit.
               The stewards agree with GIU that just because he went off track that he was not
               obligated to adopt a cool down or prep strategy for the remainder of the lap. GIU
               stated that he was pushing and that as such he was not liable for impeding. GIU had
               the right to continue to push, however his telemetry at Turn 3 with CHO directly behind
               was not consistent with a car that was continuing to push. Under the circumstances,
               the Stewards determine that GIU unnecessarily impeded CHO at T3. The penalty
               imposed is specified by the penalty guidelines and is consistent with past precedents
               for similar infractions.

               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     5 - Gabriel Bortoleto
Competitor Audi Revolut F1 Team
Time            15:06
Session         Race
Fact            Car 5 left the track in turn 11
Infringement Alleged breach of Article B1.8.6 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, and in-car video
                evidence.
                At the entry to turn 11, Car 5 (Gabriel Bortoleto) moved to overtake Car 43 (Franco
                Colapinto) on the outside. Car 43 stayed alongside and in that battle Car 5 left the
                edge of the track and rejoined ahead of Car 43.
                Under the Driving Standards Guidelines, had the front axle of Car 5 been ahead at
                the apex, Car 5 would have been entitled to racing room on the inside. There was no
                racing room on the inside which explained why Car 5 left the edge of the track. Had
                the front axle of Car 43 been ahead of the front axle of Car 5 at the apex, Car 43 was
                not obliged to leave racing room on the outside.
                The Stewards were unable, by reference to the available evidence, to reach a level of
                comfortable satisfaction as to which of the two cars was ahead at the apex and in
                these circumstances determined to take no further action.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

                Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely
                on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

                approach of Car 18.

                at the time the driver took the decision to commence that procedure, the proximity of
                Car 18 would not have been obvious to him.
                The situation was compounded by the fact that the pit lane exit road (as marked)
                requires cars performing practice starts to merge with cars travelling down the fast
                lane directly to the pit exit, over a very short distance.
                The Stewards noted that although the driver of Car 18 had to brake, the situation was

Infringement Breach of Article B1.8.5 of the FIA F1 Regulations.
Decision        Driver: Formal warning.
Reason          The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 6 (Isack Hadjar), the team representative
                of Car 6 and reviewed video evidence.
                On the approach to Turn 1, Car 23 moved to the outside of the corner on the
                approach of Car 6, to avoid any impeding of that car. The driver of Car 6 locked
                brakes and had to abort the lap. He was obviously upset with this and took what could
                be described as “retaliatory action” by swerving towards Car 23.
                The Stewards regard this as not only erratic but also an action that should be
                discouraged and hence impose the penalty of a warning to the driver. Had the action
                been dangerous or resulted in a collision, a more severe penalty would have been
                imposed.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

                Decisions of the Stewards are taken independently of the FIA and are based solely
                on the relevant regulations, guidelines and evidence presented.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     14 - Martinius Stenshorne
Competitor Rodin Motorsport
Time            16:18
Session         Qualifying
Fact            Car 14 (Stenshorne) allegedly impeded Car 11 (Montoya) at Turn 12.
Infringement Alleged breach of Article 31.6 of the FIA Formula 2 Sporting Regulations.
Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Documents 13 & 14) and heard the Drivers of Car 14
                (Stenshorne) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined
                video and marshalling sector times.
                The driver of Car 14 explained that both cars were on a warm-up lap and that he was
                attempting to create a gap ahead in preparation for his push lap. The driver of Car 11
                agreed that both cars were on a warm-up lap but acknowledged that he was
                attempting to overtake Car 14 in order to secure a more favourable track position for
                his push lap.
                Marshalling sector times confirmed that both cars were running in sequence and were
                on warm-up laps at the time of the incident. Accordingly, the Stewards determined that
                Car 14 did not unnecessarily impede Car 11 and therefore decided that no further
                action was warranted.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
                Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver     14 - Hiyu Yamakoshi
Competitor Van Amersfoort Racing
Time            15:30
Session         Qualifying
Fact            Mechanics of Car 14 (Yamakoshi) worked on the car after the end-of-race signal had
                been issued.
Infringement Breach of Article 44.3 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.
             Breach of Article 2.5.1 of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision        - Car 14 is disqualified from the Qualifying session.
                - All lap times set during the session are deleted.
                - Car 14 is granted permission to start both the Sprint and Feature races from the
                back of the grid.
Reason          The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Driver of
                Car 14 (Yamakoshi) and the Team Representative (Document 17).
                Video footage showed that, prior to the end-of-race signal being given, Car 14 was in
                its pit stop position and was being worked on. After the end-of-race signal was given,
                mechanics continued to work on the car for approximately a further two minutes.
                The Team Representative confirmed the facts and explained that Car 14 had
                experienced engine issues during the session and that the Driver entered the pit lane
                for repairs. He further explained that the team required assistance from the engine
                supplier to carry out the repairs; however, the repairs could not be completed before
                the end of the session. The Team Representative stated that the team then needed
                to ensure that the car could return to parc fermé under its own power and without
                assistance.
                The Stewards accept the Team's explanation and acknowledge that the Team was
                not seeking to gain any sporting advantage and was, in fact, attempting to avoid
                causing any unnecessary delay to the end-of-session procedures. Nonetheless,
                working on a car after the end-of-race signal has been given is prohibited by the
                Sporting Regulations, as parc fermé conditions commence upon the issuance of the
                end-of-race signal.
                Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards find that a breach of the
                regulations has occurred and accordingly impose the standard penalty of
                disqualification for a breach of parc fermé conditions.
                Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
              Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
             Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Fact            Car 2 (UGO) collided with Car 6 (DEP) on the front straight.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting
             Code.
Decision       Drop of five grid positions for the Sprint and Feature Races at this Event in
               accordance with Article 39.3 (g) of the FIA F3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2
               penalty points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the 2026 season = 4.
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence. They summoned and heard the Drivers and
               Team Representatives of Car 2 and Car 6 (documents 15 and 16).
               Car 6 (DEP) attempted to pass Car 2 (UGO) on the front straight with both cars
               already to the right of center of the track. UGO immediately moved right to defend,
               and continued moving toward the track edge. UGO’s defence crowded DEP beyond
               the edge of the track, at which point a collision occurred between DEP’s left front wing
               and UGO’s right rear tyre causing a puncture. UGO’s car also left the track before a
               secondary collision which resulted in DEP hitting the wall. Having considered the
               matter extensively, the Stewards determine that DEP made a legitimate pass attempt
               and that UGO’s attempted defensive move was too late. Furthermore, UGO was not
               entitled to crowd DEP beyond the edge of the track and therefore the Stewards
               conclude that UGO was wholly responsible for the collision. In determining the
               penalty, which is greater than past precedents for collisions in Free Practice, the
               Stewards considered the lateness of the move, the unjustified crowding beyond track
               limits and the fact that such vigorous defense is unnecessary within the confines of
               Free Practice.

               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (d) of the FIA International Sporting Code.
Decision       Ten seconds (10) time penalty in accordance with Article 39.3 (b) of the FIA F2
               Sporting Regulations. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for
               the 2026 season = 4 points. As Car 6 was not classified and the penalty could not be
               served during the race, it was converted to a 5 place grid drop for the next race in
               which the Driver participates.
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 25 & 26) and heard the Drivers of Car 6
               (Tsolov) and Car 11 (Montoya) and the team representatives. They examined video
               evidence, on board footage and GPS data.
               The driver of Car 6 explained that he had DRS and saw an opportunity to overtake
               Car 11 on the inside of Turn 1. He stated that, upon reaching the apex, Car 11
               moved towards the right hand side of the track, leaving insufficient room and resulting
               in contact between the two cars.
               The driver of Car 11 explained that he approached and negotiated the corner
               normally and observed Car 6 attempting a late overtaking manoeuvre. He
               acknowledged that Car 6 had achieved overlap at the apex but contended that this
               was a consequence of Car 6 carrying excessive speed into Turn 1, which forced him
               to drive on the kerb. Contact subsequently occurred between the cars during the
               corner.
               Having carefully considered the matter, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was
               overly optimistic in attempting the overtake at Turn 1. The manoeuvre was initiated
               late, and Car 6 carried excessive speed into the corner, which significantly
               contributed to the incident. The Stewards concluded that Car 6 was predominantly
               responsible for the collision and therefore elected to impose a drop of five grid
               positions for the drivers’ next race plus 2 penalty points.

               manoeuvre.

               predominantly at fault for the collision, having failed to react to his closing speed in
               relation to Car 31 and causing the collision. While Car 31 moved to the left to avoid
               the cars ahead, this did not relieve Car 25 of its responsibility to avoid the collision.
               As the incident occurred on the opening lap, the Stewards took this into account as a
               mitigating factor and imposed a five (5) second time penalty in accordance with the
               2026 FIA Formula 3 Penalty Guidelines. Since Car 25 was not classified, the penalty

Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (e) of the FIA International Sporting
             Code.
Decision       A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this
               Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the
               2026 season = 6 points
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Documents 29 & 27) and heard the Drivers of Car 6

               examined video evidence.

               follow him. He further stated that, as he approached Turn 11, he observed Car 6
               warming its tyres on the racing line. To avoid a potential collision, he took avoiding
               action and left the track.
               The Driver of Car 6 explained that he was behind Car 12 and, after seeing several
               other cars begin their laps, decided to do the same. He stated that the cars ahead
               were attempting to create a gap before starting their laps, and he therefore began
               warming his tyres. He acknowledged that there were other cars behind but admitted
               that he did not expect Car 11 to be so close until he saw it alongside him.
               Having considered the matter extensively, the Stewards determined that Car 6 was
               driving erratically by warming its tyres on the racing line while not travelling at racing
               speed. As a result, Car 11 was forced to take avoiding action and leave the track.
               The Stewards therefore determined that Car 6 hindered Car 11 and elect to impose a

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following

No / Driver    12 - Mari Boya
Competitor PREMA Racing
Time           15:23
Session        Qualifying
Fact           Car 12 (Boya) was driving unnecessarily slowly off the racing line on the approach to
               Turn 11.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2 (e) of the FIA International Sporting
             Code.
Decision       A drop of 3 places on the grid for the Sprint Race & Feature Race at this
               Competition. In addition, 2 points to be added to the driver’s record. Total for the
               2026 season = 4 points
Reason         The Stewards summoned (Document 24) and heard the Driver of Car 12 (Boya) and
               the team representative. They examined video evidence.
               During the session, Car 12, which was leading a group of cars, slowed significantly
               on the exit of Turn 10 and began warming its tyres. The driver then moved to the right-
               hand side of the track, leaving the racing line clear to the left. Several cars
               approaching from behind elected to momentarily queue behind Car 12 rather than
               continue at normal speed on the racing line.
               The speed of Car 12 reduced to approximately 31 km/h. As additional cars caught the
               group, this resulted in two and, at times, three lines of cars travelling side by side at
               low speed, including on the racing line.
               The driver of Car 12 explained that he was leading a group of cars and chose to slow
               down in order to avoid providing a tow to the cars behind. He acknowledged that he
               reduced speed significantly, including selecting first gear, but stated that he was
               travelling off the racing line at all times. He further explained that he avoided
               accelerating and braking aggressively in order to avoid driving erratically.
               The Stewards acknowledge that there are occasions during practice and qualifying
               sessions when drivers may need to slow significantly off the racing line, or even come
               to a stop, in order to avoid impeding another car. Such circumstances may constitute
               driving "necessarily" slowly.
               In this case, however, the Stewards determined that Car 12 slowed to an excessively
               low speed without a valid sporting or safety justification. The sole purpose of this
               action was to seek a sporting advantage by avoiding providing a tow and potentially
               benefiting from one later in the lap. By doing so, Car 12 contributed to the formation
                 of a queue of cars travelling at very low speed and to the circumstances that led to
                incidents involving multiple cars approaching Turn 11.
                Having carefully considered the matter, the Stewards conclude that Car 12 was
                driving unnecessarily slowly. Accordingly, they impose the standard penalty of a three
                grid place drop for both the Sprint Race and the Feature Race, together with two
                penalty points.

                Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and

                track gained a position over Car 15.

Infringement     Breach of Article 40.11 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations

Decision         Reprimand (driving) for all cars listed above.

Reason           The Stewards reviewed video, timing data, and GPS data.

                 The evidence showed that the cars listed above entered the Pit Lane
                 while the Safety Car was deployed. The Race Director had not instructed
                 the cars to use the Pit Lane, and the marshalling light panels clearly
                 indicated that the cars were to remain on the track.

                 Article 40.11 of the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations states: “Other
                 than when the cars and the safety car are required to use the pit lane, no
                 car may enter the pits whilst the safety car is deployed unless it is for the
                 purpose of changing damaged tyres, or a change of climatic conditions
                 necessitates the use of a different specification of tyre or repairing a
                 genuine accident damage.”

                 None of the exceptions permitted under Article 40.11 applied. The
                 Stewards therefore determine that each driver breached Article 40.11 of
                 the FIA Formula 3 Sporting Regulations.

                 Ordinarily, such a breach, particularly if committed by one car or a limited
                 number of cars, would warrant a more significant sporting penalty.
                 However, the Stewards note that all the cars concerned entered the Pit
                 Lane and that none stopped at their designated garage area, conducted
                 a pit stop, or derived a sporting advantage. The Stewards consider these
                 circumstances sufficiently mitigating to impose a Reprimand.

                 This decision arises from the exceptional circumstances of this incident,
                 which involved a collective failure by the drivers concerned. It should not
                 be regarded as establishing a precedent. Any similar breach in the future
                 will be assessed independently, having regard to its particular facts,
                 circumstances, and sporting consequences.

                 Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain
                 decisions of the Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA
                 International Sporting Code and Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and

The Stewards, having received a report from the Race Director, have considered the following
matter and determine the following:

No / Driver    29 - Nicola Lacorte
Competitor DAMS Lucas Oil
Time           09:08
Session        Race 2
Fact           Car 29 (Lacorte) made more than one change of direction while defending against
               Car 9 (Giusti) between Turns 5 and 6.
Infringement Breach of Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(b) of the International Sporting Code.
Decision       A ten-second time penalty, imposed in accordance with Article 39.3(b) of the FIA
               Formula 3 Sporting Regulations. In addition, two (2) penalty points are added to the
               driver’s record. The driver’s total for the 2026 season is 2 penalty points.
Reason         The Stewards examined video evidence.
               On Lap 16, after exiting Turn 5 and while approaching Turn 6, Car 29 (Lacorte) made
               two changes of direction while defending against Car 9 (Giusti). Car 29 initially moved
               to the right, away from the racing line, before subsequently moving back to the left
               towards the racing line as the cars approached the braking zone for Turn 6.
               When returning towards the racing line, Car 29 did not leave at least one car width
               between his car and the edge of the track. This movement caused Car 9 to take
               evasive action, lose traction under braking, and leave the track at Turn 6.
               Appendix L, Chapter IV, Article 2(b) of the International Sporting Code provides that
               more than one change of direction to defend a position is not permitted. It further
               provides that a driver returning towards the racing line after defending off-line must
               leave at least one car width between their car and the edge of the track on the
               approach to a corner.
               Having considered the incident in its entirety, the Stewards determined that Car 29
               made more than one change of direction while defending and was wholly responsible
               for causing Car 9 to leave the track.
               The Stewards therefore impose a ten-second time penalty. In addition, two penalty
               points are added to the driver’s record in accordance with the 2026 FIA Formula 3
               Penalty Guidelines.
               Competitors are reminded that they have the right to appeal certain decisions of the
               Stewards, in accordance with Article 15 of the FIA International Sporting Code and
               Chapter 5 of the FIA Judicial and Disciplinary Rules, within the applicable time limits.

Decision        No further action.
Reason          The Stewards summoned (Documents 47 & 48) and heard the Drivers of Car 1
                (Camara) and Car 22 (Varrone) and the team representatives. They examined video
                footage and onboard evidence.
                The Driver of Car 1 explained that, upon entering Turn 1, the cars ahead of him
                slowed more than he had anticipated. He therefore had to reduce his speed but he
                made contact with Car 3 who was ahead of him. The Driver of Car 22 explained that,
                upon entering Turn 1, he saw Car 1 ahead suddenly move to the left-hand side of the
                track while travelling at reduced speed. At the same time, Car 23 was running
                alongside him on his outside, leaving him with no available space to move further to
                the outside. The Driver of Car 22 stated that he attempted to reduce his speed as
                soon as he noticed Car 1 slowing, at the apex of Turn 2, when Car 23 made contact
                with Car 1, and ultimately Car 22 also made contact with Car 1.
                Having considered the circumstances of the incident, the Stewards considered that
                neither Driver could be considered wholly or predominantly responsible for the
                collision. Taking all the circumstances into consideration, the Stewards determined
                that Car 22 was not blame for the incident and decided that No Further Action was
                appropriate.

               the right (on the inside of Turn 1) and Car 8 attempted to overtake around the
               outside. Car 7 was immediately ahead of Car 1. The video evidence showed that the
               front axle of Car 8 was ahead of the front axle of Car 1 at the apex. Car 1
               subsequently failed to leave Car 8 sufficient racing room at the exit, resulting in Car 8
               being forced off the track.
               The driver of Car 1 stated that he considered Car 8 was not ahead at the apex and
               had therefore not earned the right to racing room at the exit. The driver of Car 8
               expressed the opposite view.
